Margaret Holloway: Right, let's start. The paper claims 31% of GSM8K test items appear near-verbatim in two open pretraining corpora. To be blunt, if that holds, half the leaderboard deltas from last year are noise.
Lin Xiaoyu: If I'm being honest, the 31% depends heavily on their 13-gram threshold. When I reran it at 8-grams last week it jumped to 44%, at 20-grams it dropped to 12%.
Rajesh Iyer: Let me push back on the framing. N-gram overlap measures exposure, not memorization. Thanks, Xiaoyu, for the sweep, but a 32-point swing tells me the metric is unstable, not that contamination is everywhere.
Kevin Zhao: To be fair to the authors, internally we see the same pattern. As the person running pretraining data dedup at Meridian, I can say our filtered mix still had roughly 6% of MMLU questions after decontamination.
Tomás Echeverría: Concretely, Kevin, is that 6% before or after you strip answer options? Because the paper only matches stems, and paraphrased stems slip through.
Kevin Zhao: Stems only. With options included it was closer to 2%. To be fair, I can't share the exact pipeline, but the dedup heuristics were written by Priya Raman on our team and they're aggressive.
Margaret Holloway: Maggie's rule in this room: a claim without a released script doesn't count. Raj, what do you think of their perplexity-gap test in section 4?
Rajesh Iyer: Let me push back again: the perplexity gap between original and paraphrased items is confounded by paraphrase quality. They used GPT-style rewrites, which are systematically lower-perplexity. You need human paraphrases as a control.
Lin Xiaoyu: I actually have human paraphrases for 500 GSM8K items from my thesis pilot. I defended my proposal on March 12 and that set was the main deliverable. Happy to share it, it's at github.com/linxy-eval/gsm-para.
Tomás Echeverría: Concretely, with Xiaoyu's set we could compute the accuracy drop on paraphrased versus original. If a model loses more than 10 points, that's a stronger signal than any n-gram count.
Kevin Zhao: We ran something similar. Our 70B checkpoint dropped 7.5 points on paraphrased GSM8K, the 8B dropped 3. Bigger models memorize more, which is the uncomfortable part for us.
Margaret Holloway: To be blunt, that scale effect is the headline the paper missed. As director of the Centre, I'd want us to write a response note around it. Kevin, can you get legal sign-off to cite those numbers?
Kevin Zhao: Probably not with exact figures. Email me at kzhao@meridian-ai.com and I'll route it to our publications review, they usually take two weeks. My direct line is +1 415-555-0187 if it gets stuck.
Rajesh Iyer: I'd rather we not depend on proprietary numbers at all. Let me push back on that plan: we build a dynamic benchmark, regenerated monthly from templates, so contamination is impossible by construction.
Tomás Echeverría: Templates have their own problem, Dr. Iyer. Models learn the template distribution. I saw this in my master's at Universidad de los Andes, our synthetic math set saturated in four months.
Lin Xiaoyu: If I'm being honest, I think both are needed: a private held-out set refreshed quarterly plus paraphrase-drop as the reported metric. Hugo Lefèvre at Mila tried this and their canary strings got scraped within a year.
Margaret Holloway: Canary strings failing is a disclosure problem. Labs should publish their decontamination reports. Kevin, would Meridian commit to that?
Kevin Zhao: To be fair, I'd personally support it. I've been pushing for it since I moved here from Beijing last October. But the competitive concern is real: the report reveals the data mix.
Rajesh Iyer: Then report aggregate overlap rates per benchmark, not sources. That reveals nothing about the mix. I'll draft a one-page proposal; my student @tomas_ech can circulate it on the workshop Slack.
Tomás Echeverría: Sure. Concretely, I'll also set up the paraphrase-drop harness; I'm in the lab at Universitätstrasse 6, 8092 Zürich most days, so ping me there or on +41 44 632 1957.
Lin Xiaoyu: I'll release the paraphrase set under CC-BY by October 1. Contact is xlin@ecle.ed.ac.uk. One caveat: 40 items have ambiguous answers and I'd drop them.
Margaret Holloway: Good. To be blunt about timelines, I'm on sabbatical from January, so the note needs to go to arXiv before Christmas. Decision: we write it, paraphrase-drop is the primary metric, n-gram overlap goes in the appendix.
Rajesh Iyer: Agreed, with one condition: we report results at three n-gram thresholds, not one. Thanks, Maggie, I'll take the related-work section.
Kevin Zhao: I'll try to get at least relative numbers cleared, 70B versus 8B drop ratio rather than raw accuracy. That's usually acceptable to our reviewers.

rows.digest:
沈若溪: 人齐了，咱们开始。怎么说呢，今天的题目有点敏感：AI翻译进了出版流程以后，译者和作者还剩多少位置。我在青禾读书会做了六年发起人，第一次见大家这么焦虑。
郭伟东: 讲句实在话，成本压力是真的。我们今年引进的12本外国小说里，有4本试了机翻加人工精修，单本翻译费从9万降到3万6。我作为蓝鲸文化的副总编辑，签字的就是我。
韩冬: 郭总，这玩意儿咋整？精修费按千字80算，比原来千字150少了一半多，可活儿一点没少，机翻那译文错得老鼻子了，我改一页得整半个钟头。
苏曼宁: 我从作者这边说。我那本《雾港纪事》去年加印时，出版方问能不能授权做AI有声书和机翻英文样章，合同里一句‘衍生技术使用’就带过了。说到底，作者根本不知道自己签了什么。
陈佩德: 呵呵，‘衍生技术使用’，这措辞可真是高明，写了跟没写一样。我们星河数字阅读平台的合同模板我看过，这一条一般藏在第十七条的附件里。
沈若溪: 怎么说呢，大家都爱拿刘慈欣的《三体》举例。英文版是刘宇昆翻的，2015年拿了雨果奖，那种再创造，机器做不了。
韩冬: 可不咋的。刘宇昆那译本加了多少注，调了多少语序，机翻能整明白吗？我去年在大连外国语大学带过一学期翻译工作坊，学生拿机翻改《三体》片段，全给整拧巴了。
郭伟东: 讲句实在话，《三体》是特例。普通类型小说的读者不挑，只要通顺就行。马尔克斯的《百年孤独》2011年拿到正式中文授权以后卖了几百万册，靠的是品牌和营销，不是每一个句子。
陈佩德: 呵呵，读者不挑？那去年豆瓣上被骂到2.9分的那个机翻版又是谁家的？郭总的眼光可真是独到。
苏曼宁: 说到底，我最担心的是署名。奥威尔的《1984》中文版有二十多个译本，读者会比较译者；可如果机翻精修只署‘编辑部’，译者这个职业就被抹掉了。我建议合同里强制写明：AI参与程度和精修人员姓名都要印在版权页上。
郭伟东: 苏老师的《雾港纪事》要是加了这一条，我们法务第一个跳起来。讲句实在话，版权页署‘AI辅助’会影响首印量，渠道一看就压价。
沈若溪: 那就看法律怎么说。2021年施行的新修订《著作权法》对AI生成内容其实没有明确规定；美国版权局倒是表过态，纯AI生成的部分不受版权保护。
韩冬: 这事儿得整明白：机翻部分要是不受保护，那精修以后的译文算谁的？算我的还是算机器的？我这人实在，有事打我电话 186-4115-2738，我把改过的稿子逐句对比给你们看。
陈佩德: 版权归属先放一边，平台这边更现实。马斯克收购推特以后裁掉了大半内容审核团队，结果大家都看到了。出版也一样，把译者全砍了，出了事谁兜底？
郭伟东: 难道我们不想用好译者吗？讲句实在话，不是我们不给钱，是市场不给钱。纸书码洋这三年掉了快三成，难道让我自掏腰包？
沈若溪: 郭总这算盘打得可真响，佩服佩服。怎么说呢，我提个折中：机翻只用于初稿和样章评估，正式出版必须由署名译者全程负责，稿费不低于千字120。
苏曼宁: 我同意沈老师。另外，韩江拿了2024年诺贝尔文学奖以后，她的英译者黛博拉·史密斯被反复拿出来讨论，说明译者本身就是作品价值的一部分。
韩冬: 说得对。我上个月3号刚跟出版社打完官司，就因为译者名被印成了封底小字。这事儿老鼻子人遇到过，就是不敢吭声。我在豆瓣的号 @冬子译事 发过全过程。
陈佩德: 呵呵，打官司，勇气可嘉。平台这边我可以推一个‘人工译者认证’标签，有标签的书首页给流量。我的工作邮箱 peter.chen@xinghe-read.com，数据看板在 xinghe-read.com/dash/peterc，大家可以申请权限。
郭伟东: 这个标签我们能接受。讲句实在话，如果有流量补贴，机翻精修的书我们可以主动标注‘AI辅助’，新书书讯里也写清楚。
苏曼宁: 那我这边的合同，‘衍生技术使用’这条我要求单列，AI有声书另签。我经纪人小罗下周会联系郭总，她手机 +86 21 6281 5539。我现在住杭州西湖区文三路477号，样书寄那边就行。
沈若溪: 好，我总结。第一，联合出一份《AI翻译使用倡议》，要求版权页标明AI参与程度和译者姓名；第二，机翻只用于初稿和样章，正式出版稿费不低于千字120；第三，星河平台试点人工译者认证标签。怎么说呢，10月15日前把草稿发我邮箱 shenruoxi@qinghe-books.org。
韩冬: 行，那我整一份机翻错误对照表，《三体》片段那份也放进去，让大伙儿瞅瞅机器到底差在哪。
陈佩德: 我没意见。不过提醒一句，倡议发出去，可别又是喝杯茶就散了，呵呵。

陈佩德: 呵呵，读者不挑？那去年豆瓣上被骂到2.9分的那个机翻版又是谁家的？郭总的眼光可真是独到。

郭伟东: 苏老师的《雾港纪事》要是加了这一条，我们法务第一个跳起来。讲句实在话，版权页署‘AI辅助’会影响首印量，渠道一看就压价。

陈佩德: 版权归属先放一边，平台这边更现实。马斯克收购推特以后裁掉了大半内容审核团队，结果大家都看到了。出版也一样，把译者全砍了，出了事谁兜底？
郭伟东: 难道我们不想用好译者吗？讲句实在话，不是我们不给钱，是市场不给钱。纸书码洋这三年掉了快三成，难道让我自掏腰包？
沈若溪: 郭总这算盘打得可真响，佩服佩服。怎么说呢，我提个折中：机翻只用于初稿和样章评估，正式出版必须由署名译者全程负责，稿费不低于千字120。
苏曼宁: 我同意沈老师。另外，韩江拿了2024年诺贝尔文学奖以后，她的英译者黛博拉·史密斯被反复拿出来讨论，说明译者本身就是作品价值的一部分。
韩冬: 说得对。我上个月3号刚跟出版社打完官司，就因为译者名被印成了封底小字。这事儿老鼻子人遇到过，就是不敢吭声。我在豆瓣的号 @冬子译事 发过全过程。
陈佩德: 呵呵，打官司，勇气可嘉。平台这边我可以推一个‘人工译者认证’标签，有标签的书首页给流量。我的工作邮箱 peter.chen@xinghe-read.com，数据看板在 xinghe-read.com/dash/peterc，大家可以申请权限。
郭伟东: 这个标签我们能接受。讲句实在话，如果有流量补贴，机翻精修的书我们可以主动标注‘AI辅助’，新书书讯里也写清楚。
苏曼宁: 那我这边的合同，‘衍生技术使用’这条我要求单列，AI有声书另签。我经纪人小罗下周会联系郭总，她手机 +86 21 6281 5539。我现在住杭州西湖区文三路477号，样书寄那边就行。
沈若溪: 好，我总结。第一，联合出一份《AI翻译使用倡议》，要求版权页标明AI参与程度和译者姓名；第二，机翻只用于初稿和样章，正式出版稿费不低于千字120；第三，星河平台试点人工译者认证标签。怎么说呢，10月15日前把草稿发我邮箱 shenruoxi@qinghe-books.org。
韩冬: 行，那我整一份机翻错误对照表，《三体》片段那份也放进去，让大伙儿瞅瞅机器到底差在哪。
陈佩德: 我没意见。不过提醒一句，倡议发出去，可别又是喝杯茶就散了，呵呵。

rows.digest:
Eleanor Whitcombe: Let's get going. Item one is the generative AI policy, which the Dean wants by November. For what it's worth, I've chaired this department for eight years and I've never seen a policy question split us this badly.
Marcus Oyelaran: Oh brilliant, another committee to draft another policy that students will ignore. With respect, we already have an academic integrity code. AI-written essays are plagiarism under the existing wording; we don't need a new document.
Daniel Reyes-Park: Quick data point. In our spring survey, 71% of undergraduates said they'd used ChatGPT on coursework at least once, and only 18% thought they'd broken a rule. From where I sit at the Centre for Teaching and Learning, the existing code is simply not being read that way.
Priyanka Desai: I'd just gently add that detection tools are not the answer. OpenAI itself withdrew its AI text classifier in 2023 because of low accuracy, and the false-positive studies show non-native English writers get flagged far more often.
Ingrid Solberg: Speaking as a writer, my worry is different. When my novel The Salt Archive came out in translation last year, I found pirated copies of it in a training dataset scrape. Students should understand that these tools are built on other people's unpaid work.
Marcus Oyelaran: Ingrid's The Salt Archive is exactly why I'm against blanket permission. With respect, if we let students run prompts on everything, we're teaching them that authorship is optional.
Eleanor Whitcombe: For what it's worth, the legal side is moving. The EU AI Act classifies AI systems used to evaluate students or determine admissions as high-risk, so any grading tool we adopt will carry compliance obligations from 2026.
Daniel Reyes-Park: And GDPR applies to anything students paste in. If a student uploads a classmate's peer review into a chatbot, that's personal data leaving the university. That's the part people forget.
Priyanka Desai: I'd just gently propose a three-tier model per assignment: AI prohibited, AI permitted with disclosure, AI required. Each syllabus marks every assignment with one tier, and students attach a short disclosure statement when they use it.
Marcus Oyelaran: Splendid, so now every essay comes with a confession form. Wonderful. Because nothing says rigorous scholarship like a checkbox. With respect, students will tick 'no AI' and move on.
Ingrid Solberg: Marcus, the checkbox isn't the point; the conversation is. Orwell's 'Politics and the English Language' argues that sloppy language enables sloppy thinking. That's the lesson: if a student can't defend a sentence in a viva, they didn't write it.
Eleanor Whitcombe: That suggests oral defence as the safeguard rather than detection. For what it's worth, the Russell Group published principles on generative AI in 2023 that lean the same way: teach AI literacy, adapt assessment, don't ban.
Priyanka Desai: I'd just gently note the workload. A ten-minute viva for each of 140 students in my second-year module is twenty-three hours. I'm up for tenure review in March, and I can't absorb that on top of my teaching load.
Daniel Reyes-Park: We could sample instead: viva 15% of submissions at random plus any flagged by the marker's judgement. The Centre can fund graduate assistants to run them. Drop me a line at d.reyespark@halden.ac.uk and I'll send the costing.
Marcus Oyelaran: Random vivas. Marvellous. Who exactly do you think gets 'flagged by judgement' first? With respect, it'll be the international students, which is the same bias Priyanka described with detectors.
Ingrid Solberg: That's fair. Then make it purely random, no discretionary flags. Speaking as a writer, I'd also want a short reflective note on process for any tier-two assignment: what the tool suggested, what you kept, what you rejected.
Eleanor Whitcombe: Good. Separately, staff use. Musk buying Twitter showed how fast a platform's terms can change; we shouldn't build marking workflows on a vendor whose terms might flip next term. Any staff tool needs a university contract.
Daniel Reyes-Park: Agreed. We have a sandboxed instance at halden-ctl.ac.uk/ai-sandbox that doesn't retain data. I set it up after moving over from the Toronto school board in 2024, and it's already compliant with our data protection review.
Priyanka Desai: I'd just gently ask that the policy protect junior staff too. If a student complains that a tier was unfair, the module convenor shouldn't carry it alone. My office is Room 3.14, Calloway Building, if anyone wants to draft that clause with me.
Marcus Oyelaran: Fine. I'll concede the tiers if tier one, AI prohibited, is the default for all first-year writing modules. With respect, students have to learn to write a paragraph unaided before they learn to edit a machine's.
Ingrid Solberg: I'll second that. And for the record, I won't be using The Salt Archive as a set text again until the publisher clarifies the licensing, so it's off the reading list either way. My agent Clara Mendes is chasing it.
Eleanor Whitcombe: Right, decisions. One: three-tier labels on every assignment, tier one default in first year. Two: no AI detectors in misconduct cases. Three: random 15% vivas, funded by the Centre. Four: process notes for tier two. Five: staff tools only through university-contracted services. Draft to me at e.whitcombe@halden.ac.uk by October 20; call 01632 960 418 if it's urgent.
Priyanka Desai: I'd just gently volunteer to draft the tier definitions. I'll circulate on the department Slack as @pdesai-lit.
Marcus Oyelaran: And I'll draft the first-year clause. Oh, and what a joy, another policy review in twelve months, I assume. With respect, put that in the minutes too.

Daniel Reyes-Park: We could sample instead: viva 15% of submissions at random plus any flagged by the marker's judgement. The Centre can fund graduate assistants to run them. Drop me a line at d.reyespark@halden.ac.uk and I'll send the costing.

Marcus Oyelaran: Random vivas. Marvellous. Who exactly do you think gets 'flagged by judgement' first? With respect, it'll be the international students, which is the same bias Priyanka described with detectors.

Ingrid Solberg: That's fair. Then make it purely random, no discretionary flags. Speaking as a writer, I'd also want a short reflective note on process for any tier-two assignment: what the tool suggested, what you kept, what you rejected.

Eleanor Whitcombe: Good. Separately, staff use. Musk buying Twitter showed how fast a platform's terms can change; we shouldn't build marking workflows on a vendor whose terms might flip next term. Any staff tool needs a university contract.

Daniel Reyes-Park: Agreed. We have a sandboxed instance at halden-ctl.ac.uk/ai-sandbox that doesn't retain data. I set it up after moving over from the Toronto school board in 2024, and it's already compliant with our data protection review.

Priyanka Desai: I'd just gently ask that the policy protect junior staff too. If a student complains that a tier was unfair, the module convenor shouldn't carry it alone. My office is Room 3.14, Calloway Building, if anyone wants to draft that clause with me.

Marcus Oyelaran: Fine. I'll concede the tiers if tier one, AI prohibited, is the default for all first-year writing modules. With respect, students have to learn to write a paragraph unaided before they learn to edit a machine's.

Ingrid Solberg: I'll second that. And for the record, I won't be using The Salt Archive as a set text again until the publisher clarifies the licensing, so it's off the reading list either way. My agent Clara Mendes is chasing it.

Eleanor Whitcombe: Right, decisions. One: three-tier labels on every assignment, tier one default in first year. Two: no AI detectors in misconduct cases. Three: random 15% vivas, funded by the Centre. Four: process notes for tier two. Five: staff tools only through university-contracted services. Draft to me at e.whitcombe@halden.ac.uk by October 20; call 01632 960 418 if it's urgent.
Priyanka Desai: I'd just gently volunteer to draft the tier definitions. I'll circulate on the department Slack as @pdesai-lit.
Marcus Oyelaran: And I'll draft the first-year clause. Oh, and what a joy, another policy review in twelve months, I assume. With respect, put that in the minutes too.

Mei Lin: Thanks for getting on, 赵工. For the record, this call is off the record and nothing goes out without your sign-off. Dave, Rachel and Jing are on with me.
赵磊: 好。说白了，我只想让这份报告被看见。LX-7电芯在45度循环测试里热失控率是0.8%，对外披露的是0.02%，差了40倍。
David Okafor: That's a headline number. Bottom line, I need to know who inside approved the 0.02% figure and whether the board saw the 0.8%.
赵磊: 质量副总刘振华6月签的字。我们BMS验证组2月就把数据报上去了，被要求'重新定义失效标准'，把冒烟不起火的不算。
Rachel Huang: To be clear, as outside counsel for Meridian I have to ask: how did you obtain the PDF? Did you breach a confidentiality agreement or access systems you weren't authorized for?
赵磊: 报告是我自己写的初稿，我有权限。我2021年4月6日入职就签了保密协议，这个我清楚。说白了，风险我认。
孙婧: Let me flag one thing: the PDF metadata shows author 'zlei' and a creation date of March 3. If HengLi checks document logs, that points straight at you.
Mei Lin: Jing's right. We won't publish the document itself, only describe it. For the record, I covered the Takata airbag recall for four years and protecting sources is the whole job.
赵磊: 那就好。之后别打我工作号，用私人号139-1762-4408，或者邮件zl_backup2026@proton.me。
David Okafor: Bottom line, one document isn't enough. We need a second independent source or HengLi's own response before we run anything.
孙婧: I used to work at CATL's Ningde lab, so I can sanity-check the test protocol. A 45°C cycle at 1C for 800 cycles is standard; 0.8% is plausible for a bad separator batch.
赵磊: 就是隔膜的问题，供应商换了一家便宜的，每平米省0.6块。苏州工业园区星湖街218号那个二号厂房的线全在用。
Rachel Huang: To be clear, we should not print the plant address or the supplier name until we have documentary confirmation. Defamation exposure in Hong Kong and PRC courts is real.
Mei Lin: Rachel, I disagree on the supplier. If the separator swap is the cause, naming it is the public-interest core. About 120,000 vehicles carry LX-7 packs.
David Okafor: Mei, I'm with Rachel for draft one. We can add the supplier in a follow-up once we have the purchase orders.
赵磊: 采购单我拿不到。不过我在github.com/zhaolei-bms放过一个公开的SOC估算工具，你们别去看，那个账号跟我真名挂钩。
孙婧: Let me flag that too, then. Zhao, please delete or privatize that repo now; the commit emails will deanonymize you within a day.
赵磊: 明白。说实话我压力很大，我老婆刚生二胎，要是被开除房贷都还不上。
Rachel Huang: Then let's talk whistleblower routes. You could file with SAMR's defect recall center in parallel. My direct line is +1 415-555-0187 if you want advice outside this group.
Mei Lin: I'll send HengLi a request for comment on Monday with a 72-hour deadline. Questions come from mlin@meridianwire.com; I'll also watch weibo.com/u/linmei_ev for any owner complaints.
孙婧: I'll pull the 2025 and 2026 owner fire reports from SAMR and the forums. If anyone tips via DM, my handle is @sunjing_checks. Let me flag: so far I count 9 thermal incidents with LX-7 packs.
David Okafor: Nine incidents plus the internal number gets us there. Bottom line: target publication October 2, contingent on legal sign-off and HengLi's response.
Rachel Huang: Agreed, with conditions: no quotes attributed to 'an engineer in the BMS team', just 'a person with direct knowledge'. That team has fewer than 15 people.
赵磊: 谢谢黄律师。说白了，只要车不再烧，我被查出来也认了。
Mei Lin: Thanks, Leo. For the record, we'll talk again Sunday at 9pm on Signal only. Delete this call log.
David Okafor: Good work, everyone. Jing, send me the incident spreadsheet by Friday.

陈志远: 各位，今天讨论的病例是赵立新，男，61岁，身份证110105196503127719，9月3日入院。说白了，就是想定一下这个病人先手术还是先做新辅助。
陈志远: 我先交代一句，我们中国医学科学院肿瘤医院胸外科这边已经评估过心肺功能，FEV1 2.1升，DLCO 78%，肺叶切除没问题。
郭佳宁: 我来汇报影像。右上肺尖后段实性结节3.8厘米，PET-CT SUVmax 11.2；4R组淋巴节短径1.4厘米，SUV 6.8，7组SUV 3.1，可疑。远处没看到转移，头颅MRI阴性。
郭佳宁: 补充一下，我8月20日刚轮转到影像科，这个片子是和刘广平老师一起复核的，7组我们俩意见不完全一致。
孙海鹰: 病理这边，CT引导穿刺是浸润性腺癌，腺泡为主。但组织条只有两条，EGFR、ALK用NGS测了阴性，PD-L1 22C3 TPS 60%。问题是4R没有病理证实，严格讲N2是影像学推断的。
林雨涵: 坦率讲，驱动基因阴性、PD-L1 60%，这是新辅助免疫联合化疗最受益的人群。CheckMate 816的数据pCR 24%，我倾向三周期纳武利尤单抗加卡铂培美曲塞。
陈志远: Grace，我同意新辅助，但说白了前提是N2得是单站。多站N2做完新辅助我们也不一定切得干净。
周明轩: 从剂量学角度，如果4R加7组都是阳性，就是多站N2，我更建议根治性同步放化疗60Gy/30次，后面接度伐利尤单抗巩固一年，PACIFIC的五年生存43%也不差。
林雨涵: 周主任，PACIFIC那批病人大部分不可切除，跟这个病人不是一回事。坦率讲，他体能状态ECOG 0，能手术就别放弃手术机会。
周明轩: 我不是反对手术。作为放疗科副主任，我只是提醒，新辅助后如果pCR没达到，术后还要不要PORT，这个要提前想好，Lung ART的结果是阴性的。
孙海鹰: 所以我坚持，先做EBUS-TBNA，把4R和7组都穿一下。我上个月刚从MD安德森进修回来，那边分期不清楚的N2基本都要求EBUS，ROSE现场评估一次就能拿到够用的组织。
陈志远: 孙老师说得对，EBUS大概一周能排上。@胸外老陈 是我的科室群账号，结果出来直接在群里@我就行。
郭佳宁: 陈主任，7组我还是觉得偏炎性，形态是扁的，有脂肪门。不过SUV 3.1确实卡在边上，我同意穿刺确认。
林雨涵: 那我先把免疫治疗前的基线检查开了：甲功、皮质醇、心肌酶、肺功能。他有20年吸烟史，每天一包，基线肺纤维化要排除，否则免疫性肺炎风险高。
林雨涵: 方案和知情同意书我发邮件给大家，lin.yuhan@pumch-onc.cn，有意见直接回。坦率讲，这周最好定下来，病人家属很焦虑。
周明轩: 从剂量学角度再说一句，如果最后走放化疗，V20要控制在30%以下，他的肺功能扛得住。我写的勾画模板放在github.com/dr-zhoumx上了，需要可以参考。
孙海鹰: 还有一点，新辅助后的标本请一定送我们这边做主要病理缓解评估，残留活性肿瘤≤10%才算MPR，取材要按IASLC推荐全瘤床取。
孙海鹰: 我平时在weibo.com/u/5832017746发一些病理科普，MPR取材规范也写过一篇，年轻医生可以看看。
郭佳宁: 疗效评估我建议每两周期复查一次增强CT，按RECIST 1.1，必要时第三周期后再做一次PET。我那对双胞胎刚上一年级，这两周下午可能要早走，复查读片我会提前排好。
陈志远: 小郭你放心。说白了，三周期后如果降期到N0或单站N1，我们就做胸腔镜右上肺叶切除加系统性淋巴结清扫。
周明轩: 如果EBUS证实4R和7组双阳性，我希望这个病例转回放疗科评估，不要硬上新辅助再手术。这点请陈主任记录在会诊意见里。
林雨涵: 我可以接受这个分支。但多站N2也有ESMO数据支持新辅助后手术，坦率讲指南给的是2B类，不是禁忌。
陈志远: 好，联系方式我确认一下：患者本人电话139-1024-5867，住址北京市朝阳区安贞里三区12号楼2单元501，主要联系人是他女儿赵晓雯。
郭佳宁: 影像科的预约有问题可以打我手机+86 138-1177-4402，晚上也能接。
孙海鹰: EBUS标本我要求至少三针，一针做ROSE，两针留NGS补测，KRAS G12C和MET 14外显子跳跃这次没覆盖到，要补。
陈志远: 最后总结：先EBUS分期；单站N2走三周期新辅助免疫化疗后手术；多站N2转放疗科评估同步放化疗。九周后MDT再讨论一次，谢谢Grace、周主任、孙老师和小郭。

周明轩: 我不是反对手术。作为放疗科副主任，我只是提醒，新辅助后如果pCR没达到，术后还要不要PORT，这个要提前想好，Lung ART的结果是阴性的。
孙海鹰: 所以我坚持，先做EBUS-TBNA，把4R和7组都穿一下。我上个月刚从MD安德森进修回来，那边分期不清楚的N2基本都要求EBUS，ROSE现场评估一次就能拿到够用的组织。
陈志远: 孙老师说得对，EBUS大概一周能排上。@胸外老陈 是我的科室群账号，结果出来直接在群里@我就行。
郭佳宁: 陈主任，7组我还是觉得偏炎性，形态是扁的，有脂肪门。不过SUV 3.1确实卡在边上，我同意穿刺确认。
林雨涵: 那我先把免疫治疗前的基线检查开了：甲功、皮质醇、心肌酶、肺功能。他有20年吸烟史，每天一包，基线肺纤维化要排除，否则免疫性肺炎风险高。
林雨涵: 方案和知情同意书我发邮件给大家，lin.yuhan@pumch-onc.cn，有意见直接回。坦率讲，这周最好定下来，病人家属很焦虑。
周明轩: 从剂量学角度再说一句，如果最后走放化疗，V20要控制在30%以下，他的肺功能扛得住。我写的勾画模板放在github.com/dr-zhoumx上了，需要可以参考。
孙海鹰: 还有一点，新辅助后的标本请一定送我们这边做主要病理缓解评估，残留活性肿瘤≤10%才算MPR，取材要按IASLC推荐全瘤床取。
孙海鹰: 我平时在weibo.com/u/5832017746发一些病理科普，MPR取材规范也写过一篇，年轻医生可以看看。
郭佳宁: 疗效评估我建议每两周期复查一次增强CT，按RECIST 1.1，必要时第三周期后再做一次PET。我那对双胞胎刚上一年级，这两周下午可能要早走，复查读片我会提前排好。
陈志远: 小郭你放心。说白了，三周期后如果降期到N0或单站N1，我们就做胸腔镜右上肺叶切除加系统性淋巴结清扫。
周明轩: 如果EBUS证实4R和7组双阳性，我希望这个病例转回放疗科评估，不要硬上新辅助再手术。这点请陈主任记录在会诊意见里。
林雨涵: 我可以接受这个分支。但多站N2也有ESMO数据支持新辅助后手术，坦率讲指南给的是2B类，不是禁忌。
陈志远: 好，联系方式我确认一下：患者本人电话139-1024-5867，住址北京市朝阳区安贞里三区12号楼2单元501，主要联系人是他女儿赵晓雯。
郭佳宁: 影像科的预约有问题可以打我手机+86 138-1177-4402，晚上也能接。
孙海鹰: EBUS标本我要求至少三针，一针做ROSE，两针留NGS补测，KRAS G12C和MET 14外显子跳跃这次没覆盖到，要补。
陈志远: 最后总结：先EBUS分期；单站N2走三周期新辅助免疫化疗后手术；多站N2转放疗科评估同步放化疗。九周后MDT再讨论一次，谢谢Grace、周主任、孙老师和小郭。

rows.digest:
林国栋: 好，人到齐了我们开始。今天就一件事：Hollis这笔380万的乡村教育专项怎么分。说到底，钱不多，不能撒胡椒面。
苏晓雯: 我讲个数据：赫章、威宁两个县我们跟踪的42所村小，教师流失率去年是31%。我的方案是60%投教师补贴，25%做数字化课程，15%留给评估和应急。
何建平: 账面上看，60%做补贴等于每年228万的经常性支出，这笔钱只有两年期限，第三年补贴断了老师照样走。作为财务总监，我不能签一个没有退出路径的预算。
陈明哲: Frankly, the evidence is on the program team's side here. Our RCT across 96 schools in Yunnan showed retention subsidies cut turnover by 40%, and as a senior fellow at PIRD I've seen the tech-first pilots mostly end up as dusty tablets.
Sarah Whitfield: From where we sit, the trust cares about measurable learning outcomes, not just headcount. I joined Hollis Family Trust only in June, but our board already asked me why the 2024 cohort reported no test-score data.
林国栋: Sarah这个问题问得对。我当年在赫章当了六年代课老师，知道考试数据在村小有多难拿。晓雯，评估这块15%够不够？
苏晓雯: 15%是57万，够做基线和终期两次测评。我讲个数据：去年我们用开源工具做的测评，成本是每生18块，代码都在github.com/sophiesu-edu上，Sarah可以让你们的人看。
何建平: 测评我没意见。我4月8日才接手财务部，上任第一件事就是发现2024年有11万的补贴发到了已经离职的老师卡上。账面上看，发放环节的风控比比例更要紧。
陈明哲: That's a fair point, 何会计. Frankly, leakage is the number one killer of cash-transfer programs. Bottom line: pay through the county education bureau payroll, not through school principals.
苏晓雯: 走教育局工资系统我们试过，到账要拖三个月。黑水沟小学的杨秀英校长上学期就因为这个垫了四万多自己的钱。
林国栋: 杨校长那个学校我去过，地址是贵州省毕节市赫章县珠市乡黑水沟村，冬天孩子上课还穿单鞋。说到底，我们得让钱比冬天先到。
何建平: 那我提个折中：补贴由基金会直接打卡，但每季度要和教育局在岗名单核对。上次为了补发，杨校长的身份证号是520527197803154421，这种信息以后不能再在群里传了。
Sarah Whitfield: From where we sit, quarterly reconciliation would satisfy our compliance team. Please loop me in directly, my cell is +1 415-555-0182 while I'm still sorting out a Shanghai number.
陈明哲: One more thing on the digital piece. My daughter just started at a boarding school in Kunming, and frankly the offline video lessons there work far better than the live-streamed ones. I'd cut the 25% to 15% and go offline-first.
苏晓雯: 我不同意砍到15%。我上个月刚从哥伦比亚TC读完在职硕士，论文就是做离线课程的，内容制作的成本主要在前期，砍了就做不出完整的三年级数学包。
林国栋: 陈博士你和晓雯会后单独对一下数字化的预算明细。老何，你算一下如果补贴降到50%，第三年用什么接上。
何建平: 账面上看，有两条路：一是用我们的留本基金收益，每年大概40万；二是第二年起要求县财政配套30%。我更倾向后者，配套写进协议。细表我发大家邮箱，有问题直接找我 hejp@chunhui-edu.org。
Sarah Whitfield: Thanks, 何会计. A county match would actually make this much easier to renew. From where we sit, a co-funding commitment is the strongest signal of sustainability we can show our trustees.
陈明哲: I'd add a caution: county matches in Weining have a history of slipping. Bottom line, make the second tranche conditional on the match actually arriving. Send me the draft at mchen@pird.org and I'll mark it up.
苏晓雯: 我同意把第二笔款和配套挂钩。另外有个情况：威宁有位老师在微博上实名吐槽补贴拖欠，主页是weibo.com/u/5823019944，已经有两千多转发了，得尽快回应。
林国栋: 这个我来处理，我用@laolin_edu那个号发个说明。说到底，透明比公关有用。晓雯你把联系方式给那位老师。
苏晓雯: 好的，让她直接打我手机139-1022-7745，我这周都在毕节。
Sarah Whitfield: Before we close, I need a decision I can take back. Is the split 50/20/15 with a 15% reserve? Our trustees meet on October 9.
林国栋: 那就定下来：教师补贴50%，数字化课程20%，评估15%，应急储备15%；补贴由基金会直发、季度核对；第二笔款以县财政30%配套到位为前提。有没有反对？
何建平: 没有反对，但我保留意见：应急储备没花完的部分，第三年必须优先转为补贴接续，这个要写进会议纪要。
陈明哲: Agreed. Frankly, it's a stronger design than what most foundations fund. PIRD can do the external evaluation pro bono for the baseline.

苏晓雯: 我讲个数据：赫章、威宁两个县我们跟踪的42所村小，教师流失率去年是31%。我的方案是60%投教师补贴，25%做数字化课程，15%留给评估和应急。
何建平: 账面上看，60%做补贴等于每年228万的经常性支出，这笔钱只有两年期限，第三年补贴断了老师照样走。作为财务总监，我不能签一个没有退出路径的预算。

陈明哲: Frankly, the evidence is on the program team's side here. Our RCT across 96 schools in Yunnan showed retention subsidies cut turnover by 40%, and as a senior fellow at PIRD I've seen the tech-first pilots mostly end up as dusty tablets.

Sarah Whitfield: From where we sit, the trust cares about measurable learning outcomes, not just headcount. I joined Hollis Family Trust only in June, but our board already asked me why the 2024 cohort reported no test-score data.
林国栋: Sarah这个问题问得对。我当年在赫章当了六年代课老师，知道考试数据在村小有多难拿。晓雯，评估这块15%够不够？
苏晓雯: 15%是57万，够做基线和终期两次测评。我讲个数据：去年我们用开源工具做的测评，成本是每生18块，代码都在github.com/sophiesu-edu上，Sarah可以让你们的人看。
何建平: 测评我没意见。我4月8日才接手财务部，上任第一件事就是发现2024年有11万的补贴发到了已经离职的老师卡上。账面上看，发放环节的风控比比例更要紧。
陈明哲: That's a fair point, 何会计. Frankly, leakage is the number one killer of cash-transfer programs. Bottom line: pay through the county education bureau payroll, not through school principals.
苏晓雯: 走教育局工资系统我们试过，到账要拖三个月。黑水沟小学的杨秀英校长上学期就因为这个垫了四万多自己的钱。
林国栋: 杨校长那个学校我去过，地址是贵州省毕节市赫章县珠市乡黑水沟村，冬天孩子上课还穿单鞋。说到底，我们得让钱比冬天先到。
何建平: 那我提个折中：补贴由基金会直接打卡，但每季度要和教育局在岗名单核对。上次为了补发，杨校长的身份证号是520527197803154421，这种信息以后不能再在群里传了。
Sarah Whitfield: From where we sit, quarterly reconciliation would satisfy our compliance team. Please loop me in directly, my cell is +1 415-555-0182 while I'm still sorting out a Shanghai number.

陈明哲: One more thing on the digital piece. My daughter just started at a boarding school in Kunming, and frankly the offline video lessons there work far better than the live-streamed ones. I'd cut the 25% to 15% and go offline-first.
苏晓雯: 我不同意砍到15%。我上个月刚从哥伦比亚TC读完在职硕士，论文就是做离线课程的，内容制作的成本主要在前期，砍了就做不出完整的三年级数学包。
林国栋: 陈博士你和晓雯会后单独对一下数字化的预算明细。老何，你算一下如果补贴降到50%，第三年用什么接上。
何建平: 账面上看，有两条路：一是用我们的留本基金收益，每年大概40万；二是第二年起要求县财政配套30%。我更倾向后者，配套写进协议。细表我发大家邮箱，有问题直接找我 hejp@chunhui-edu.org。

Sarah Whitfield: Thanks, 何会计. A county match would actually make this much easier to renew. From where we sit, a co-funding commitment is the strongest signal of sustainability we can show our trustees.

陈明哲: I'd add a caution: county matches in Weining have a history of slipping. Bottom line, make the second tranche conditional on the match actually arriving. Send me the draft at mchen@pird.org and I'll mark it up.
苏晓雯: 我同意把第二笔款和配套挂钩。另外有个情况：威宁有位老师在微博上实名吐槽补贴拖欠，主页是weibo.com/u/5823019944，已经有两千多转发了，得尽快回应。
林国栋: 这个我来处理，我用@laolin_edu那个号发个说明。说到底，透明比公关有用。晓雯你把联系方式给那位老师。
苏晓雯: 好的，让她直接打我手机139-1022-7745，我这周都在毕节。
Sarah Whitfield: Before we close, I need a decision I can take back. Is the split 50/20/15 with a 15% reserve? Our trustees meet on October 9.
林国栋: 那就定下来：教师补贴50%，数字化课程20%，评估15%，应急储备15%；补贴由基金会直发、季度核对；第二笔款以县财政30%配套到位为前提。有没有反对？
何建平: 没有反对，但我保留意见：应急储备没花完的部分，第三年必须优先转为补贴接续，这个要写进会议纪要。
陈明哲: Agreed. Frankly, it's a stronger design than what most foundations fund. PIRD can do the external evaluation pro bono for the baseline.

rows.digest:
叶秋萍: 各位，开始吧。今天两个议题：新能源车充电设施怎么进老旧小区，以及城市更新里居民怎么参与。从数据上看，国家统计局公布2024年新能源汽车产量超过1300万辆，需求已经不是问题，问题在落地。
邵立平: 我先讲市里的口径。国务院《新能源汽车产业发展规划（2021—2035年）》提出要加快充换电基础设施建设，我们滨江今年的目标是老旧小区新增8000个公共充电桩，财政按每桩补贴2000元。
戴振宇: To be honest，8000个桩，电网扛得住吗？老小区变压器容量普遍只有400千伏安，晚上七点一齐充，跳闸是分分钟的事。我们启澜储能做的就是社区侧储能柜，白天谷电存、晚上放。
Helen Varga: From a policy standpoint, the EU's Alternative Fuels Infrastructure Regulation sets mandatory charger density along core roads. But residential retrofit is left to member states, and that's exactly where the bottleneck is. In my years at Northbridge Urban Institute I've seen Amsterdam solve it with on-request public chargers.
梁家豪: 老实讲，居民那边问题唔系技术，系车位。老小区一百户才二十个车位，装了桩谁用？邵主任那篇《城市更新要有温度》讲得好好听，但落到楼下就是吵架。
邵立平: 梁先生说得有道理。所以我们打算推‘共享桩’：私人桩错峰开放，物业统一结算。我在市发改委分管能源这块三年，最难的就是物业不愿意担责任。
叶秋萍: 从数据上看，共享桩的利用率能到多少？我们学院去年在滨江大学周边做过调查，私桩平均每天空置18个小时。
戴振宇: Oh great，又一个试点。To be honest，前年那批‘智慧社区’试点，挂牌那天领导来剪彩，第二年设备全落灰，真是‘可持续’得很啊。
Helen Varga: Daniel has a point, though. From a policy standpoint, pilots fail when there's no operating budget after year one. The fix is to tie subsidies to utilisation, not installation. Pay per kilowatt-hour delivered, not per charger built.
邵立平: 按度电补贴这个思路我们可以研究。不过财政口径要跟省里对齐，我下周去省发改委汇报。有方案可以发我办公室邮箱 shaolp@binjiangdrc.gov.cn。
梁家豪: 说到城市更新，老实讲，拆了建、建了拆，街坊早就怕了。我细个喺深水埗长大，见过太多旧楼重建之后原居民根本返唔来。滨江的海湾片区唔好再行呢条路。
叶秋萍: 梁先生提到的是原地安置率。从数据上看，住建部2021年发布的《关于在实施城市更新行动中防止大拆大建问题的通知》规定拆除建筑面积原则上不应大于现状总建筑面积的20%，就是在回应这个。
Helen Varga: In Europe, the New European Bauhaus initiative pushes the same idea: renovate first, demolish last. From a policy standpoint, the carbon math supports it, since embodied carbon in demolition can wipe out decades of operational savings.
戴振宇: 所以我建议改造和储能打包：外墙保温、屋顶光伏、楼下储能柜一起做。To be honest，单做充电桩不赚钱，打包以后合同能源管理才算得过来账，回收期能从九年压到六年。
邵立平: 这个思路跟市里的方向一致。我去年在市委党校讲《城市更新要有温度》的时候也说过，改造要算碳账，也要算民生账。
梁家豪: 邵主任的演讲稿当然写得漂亮，佢讲‘温度’，街坊感受到的是‘温度计’——一量就知冷暖。老实讲，我建议每个更新项目设居民议事会，方案要有三分之二住户签字同意先至可以动工。
叶秋萍: 三分之二这个门槛，从数据上看是合理的。我们做过模拟，门槛到75%以上项目基本推不动，低于50%就会出群体投诉。我研究的那个片区，我自己也住在里面，海湾路36弄，所以感受很直接。
Helen Varga: I'd add one thing: publish the data. The World Health Organization's housing and health guidelines link cold indoor temperatures to excess winter deaths, so insulation retrofits are a health policy too. Make that case publicly and residents buy in. My contact is h.varga@northbridge-urban.org.
戴振宇: 数据我们可以提供，储能柜的运行数据实时上传到 qilan-energy.cn/open/binjiang。To be honest，政府愿意签五年运营协议，我们就愿意先垫资，第一批做三个小区。电话 137-1029-6684 找我。
邵立平: 五年协议要过人大财经委，我尽量争取。不过各位，今天讲的不代表市里正式立场，请不要外传。
梁家豪: 放心，今日讲咩，出咗门就冇人记得，呢个我哋最熟。老实讲，我只希望议事会唔系摆设。我嘅公众号 @海湾街坊志 会跟进，但唔会点名。
叶秋萍: 好，我总结。第一，充电桩补贴从按桩改为按度电，挂钩利用率；第二，私桩错峰共享，物业统一结算；第三，改造、光伏、储能打包做合同能源管理，先做三个小区试点；第四，更新项目设居民议事会，三分之二住户同意才动工。纪要10月8日前发大家。
Helen Varga: Agreed. From a policy standpoint, I'd also benchmark against the EU AI Act only where smart-grid software is involved; for most of this, it's not relevant. Thanks, Qiuping.

邵立平: 这个思路跟市里的方向一致。我去年在市委党校讲《城市更新要有温度》的时候也说过，改造要算碳账，也要算民生账。
梁家豪: 邵主任的演讲稿当然写得漂亮，佢讲‘温度’，街坊感受到的是‘温度计’——一量就知冷暖。老实讲，我建议每个更新项目设居民议事会，方案要有三分之二住户签字同意先至可以动工。
叶秋萍: 三分之二这个门槛，从数据上看是合理的。我们做过模拟，门槛到75%以上项目基本推不动，低于50%就会出群体投诉。我研究的那个片区，我自己也住在里面，海湾路36弄，所以感受很直接。

Helen Varga: I'd add one thing: publish the data. The World Health Organization's housing and health guidelines link cold indoor temperatures to excess winter deaths, so insulation retrofits are a health policy too. Make that case publicly and residents buy in. My contact is h.varga@northbridge-urban.org.
戴振宇: 数据我们可以提供，储能柜的运行数据实时上传到 qilan-energy.cn/open/binjiang。To be honest，政府愿意签五年运营协议，我们就愿意先垫资，第一批做三个小区。电话 137-1029-6684 找我。
邵立平: 五年协议要过人大财经委，我尽量争取。不过各位，今天讲的不代表市里正式立场，请不要外传。
梁家豪: 放心，今日讲咩，出咗门就冇人记得，呢个我哋最熟。老实讲，我只希望议事会唔系摆设。我嘅公众号 @海湾街坊志 会跟进，但唔会点名。
叶秋萍: 好，我总结。第一，充电桩补贴从按桩改为按度电，挂钩利用率；第二，私桩错峰共享，物业统一结算；第三，改造、光伏、储能打包做合同能源管理，先做三个小区试点；第四，更新项目设居民议事会，三分之二住户同意才动工。纪要10月8日前发大家。
Helen Varga: Agreed. From a policy standpoint, I'd also benchmark against the EU AI Act only where smart-grid software is involved; for most of this, it's not relevant. Thanks, Qiuping.

rows.digest:
陈思远: 好，开始吧。今天两件事：定价改版和A轮。说白了，这两件事是一件事——定价讲不清楚，投资人不会买单。Mike，谢谢你今天专门从上海过来。
Michael Grant: Happy to be here, Simon. As a partner at Redwood Harbor Ventures I've seen maybe forty SaaS decks this year, and the pattern is clear: pure per-seat pricing is getting punished in diligence. Investors want usage-driven expansion revenue.
林慧: 坦率讲，我们现在ARR是1,850万人民币，NRR只有96%。如果全面切到按用量计费，前两个季度收入会掉，我测算大概掉12%到15%。
周婷: 掉15%我扛不住。我们销售团队14个人，季度目标都是按席位定的。Honestly，客户的采购流程也是按席位审批的，尤其是国企客户，用量这种不确定的数字过不了预算。
赵磊: 本质上用量计费技术上不难，计量服务两周能上线。但账单系统要重写，我估计6个人月。原型代码我放在 github.com/zhaolei-dev/metering-poc 了，大家可以看。
陈思远: 磊哥，6个人月是不是保守了？我们四季度还要交付招行那个私有化项目，人手够吗？
赵磊: 不保守。私有化那边已经占了我一半人。我7月1日才入职，第一周就说过：本质上，这个团队最缺的是计费和数据平台的人，不是前端。
林慧: 我补充融资这边。A轮目标融8000万人民币，投前估值4.5亿。按现在每月烧420万的速度，现金只够撑到明年4月。坦率讲，窗口不大，最晚12月要签TS。
Michael Grant: That runway is the real issue, Helen. Bottom line, I'd rather see a hybrid model: keep a platform fee per seat, add a usage tier above a threshold. That gives you a clean expansion story without blowing up Q4 revenue.
周婷: 混合模式我能卖。我昨天刚跟国家电网江苏公司的采购李处长聊过，他们能接受平台费加超量部分。他手机是139-1234-5678，下周我约他和陈总一起见。
陈思远: 好。婷婷，这个号码别到处发。说白了，大客户关系必须收进公司CRM，不能只躺在你个人微信里，人一走客户就没了。
周婷: 收到。Honestly，我做了九年企业销售，以前在用友带华东区，这种客户关系一向是跟人走的。不过我同意录进CRM，月底前完成。
林慧: 说到估值，我和两家机构谈过。高榕那边的对接人是Jessica Wu，邮箱 jessica.wu@gaorong-example.com，她们对4.5亿有异议，认为最多3.8亿。
Michael Grant: 3.8 is a lowball. Bottom line, if you can show NRR above 110% by end of Q1 on the hybrid model, I can push my IC to lead at 4.5. You can reach me directly at +1 415-555-0142 if anyone from their side calls you.
赵磊: NRR到110%需要产品配合。本质上是要做usage dashboard，让客户自己看到用了多少、超了多少。前端我外包给了一个独立开发者 @pixel_nomad，十月底能交。
林慧: 外包合同我要先审，上次那家外包的发票问题还没处理完。纸质合同寄到浦东新区祖冲之路2290号3号楼5层，写我名字。
陈思远: Mike，还有董事会席位的问题。领投方要一个席位的话，我和Leo、Helen三个创始人还能保住多数吗？
Michael Grant: Five-seat board: three founders, one lead investor, one independent. That's standard. Bottom line, my concern is less governance and more that you're still the only person who can close state-owned enterprises, Simon.
周婷: 这点我不同意。现在国企客户60%是我团队独立签下的，陈总只参加最后一轮谈判。Honestly，Mike你看的是去年的数据。
陈思远: 数据上婷婷说得对。作为创始人兼CEO，我的时间应该放在融资和产品上。说白了，下半年我不再亲自跑单，销售全权交给婷婷。
林慧: 那我记一下决议：一，定价改为平台费加用量阶梯，10月15日起对新客户生效，老客户续约时迁移。二，A轮按4.5亿推，Mike这边牵头，高榕作为备选。坦率讲，我还是担心老客户迁移会有流失。
赵磊: 老客户我建议给六个月价格保护。技术上计量先shadow跑一个月，不出账单只出报告。另外我的双胞胎下个月出生，十一月我要休两周陪产假，提前说一下。
Michael Grant: Congratulations, Leo. Plan around it. I'll send the term sheet draft to helen.lin@jiguangshuzhan.com by Friday, and Dr. Patel from our portfolio team will run the commercial diligence.
周婷: 销售这边我下周一出新报价单和佣金方案：平台费拿基础提成，用量部分单独算。我在 weibo.com/u/tinazhou_sales 上有不少国企IT负责人关注，到时候发个预告。
陈思远: 微博先别发，等定价正式上线再说。好，分工：林姐负责纪要和TS，磊哥负责计量上线，婷婷负责报价单。下次会9月25日同一时间。
林慧: 收到，纪要今晚发。另外我9月30日要去新加坡见两家美元基金做备选，那周的付款审批找陈总签。

rows.digest:
周文涛: 各位好，今天按Chatham House规则。我们院在东城区东四十条甲22号，会后材料我会发到群里。CBAM明年1月1日进入definitive period，今天主要讨论钢铁出口怎么应对。
马国栋: 说白了，钢铁是第一个挨刀的。作为副秘书长我直接给数字：2025年对欧钢材出口大约380万吨，按默认值算，每吨要多付60到90欧元，长流程企业利润基本被吃光。
刘芳: 坦率讲，默认值本身就有问题。欧盟用的是本国排放最差10%的水平，对中国企业带有惩罚性。我们研究院建议推动中欧在MRV方法学上互认，而不是被动接受default values。
Sarah Whitfield: Frankly, the UK is launching its own CBAM in January 2027, so as first secretary at the British Embassy I'm here partly to listen. I spent six years at DG TAXUD before this posting, so I know how Brussels thinks about default values.
陈立言: 从计量角度看，问题在于数据颗粒度。我们组的测算显示，如果企业能提交实测排放数据，平均碳强度是每吨钢1.9吨CO2，比欧盟默认值低约18%。模型和数据都放在github.com/chenly-carbon上了。
周文涛: 马总，你们协会的会员企业有多少真正具备实测核算能力？这是关键。
马国栋: 说白了，大厂没问题，中小厂一塌糊涂。我们钢协摸底了127家，能出第三方核查报告的不到40家。宝武的李卫东副总上周还跟我说，核查费一家就要30万。
刘芳: 我3月12日刚调到研究院，之前在条法司做WTO争端。坦率讲，CBAM在WTO框架下有GATT第20条的空间，起诉胜算不大，更现实的是谈判换取全国碳市场价格的抵扣认可。
Sarah Whitfield: On the carbon price deduction: the EU will only credit an explicit carbon price actually paid. China's ETS allowance price is around 90 yuan, versus 70-plus euros in the EU. Frankly, the gap is too big for a meaningful deduction unless steel enters the national ETS soon.
陈立言: 钢铁纳入全国碳市场预计2027年开始配额分配。我上个月刚结束在鲁汶大学的访问学者回来，欧方学者普遍认为免费配额比例才是谈判焦点，而不是碳价绝对值。
周文涛: Thanks, Sarah. 那英国的UK CBAM会不会和欧盟做linking？如果英欧两套核算规则不一样，企业合规成本要翻倍。
Sarah Whitfield: Linking is on the table; ministers will decide after the ETS linking talks conclude. If your members have specific questions, email me at sarah.whitfield@fcdo.gov.uk or call the economic section on +86 10 5192 4000.
马国栋: 我提个具体要求：协会想办一个中英CBAM合规对接会，11月在唐山。我手机139-1024-6658，Sarah你那边能不能牵个线，请英国钢铁协会的人来？
刘芳: 我反对把重点放在合规上。坦率讲，合规越顺利，等于默认了这个机制的合法性。我们应该在COP31和中欧经贸高层对话上把它定性为单边贸易措施。
陈立言: 刘处，我不太同意。从计量角度看，拒绝合规的代价是企业直接按默认值交钱，2026年就是真金白银的损失。两条腿走路：一边谈判，一边帮中小企业建数据体系。
周文涛: 我同意立言的看法。我们院打算做一个公开的企业碳足迹计算工具，进展我会在weibo.com/u/5823046117上更新，大家也可以关注@zhouwt_climate。
马国栋: 说白了，还有一个出路是转口和产业转移。已经有企业在越南、马来西亚建轧钢线，把最终加工放在第三国，但欧盟反规避条款会盯上，风险很大。
Sarah Whitfield: That route worries Brussels most. The anti-circumvention clause covers slight modifications in third countries. I'd strongly advise members not to rely on it.
刘芳: 这恰恰说明欧方规则在不断扩张。我们研究院的建议稿会写三点：争取过渡期延长、要求方法学互认、把CBAM收入的一部分用于支持发展中国家减排。
陈立言: Dr. Chen这个称呼我在欧洲用惯了，哈哈。补一个数据：电炉钢的碳强度只有长流程的三分之一，如果对欧出口转向电炉钢产品，CBAM成本能降低60%以上，这是结构性答案。
周文涛: 老周我插一句私事：我女儿今年刚去鹿特丹读港口物流，她说欧洲进口商已经开始要求中国供应商提前报碳数据了，市场比政策走得快。
马国栋: 电炉钢的问题是废钢不够、电价太高。说白了，没有绿电价格支持，电炉转型就是空话。协会会向发改委提绿电直供的试点建议。
Sarah Whitfield: Frankly, bottom line from our side: the UK wants a predictable, data-based system and is open to technical cooperation on MRV. A joint UK-China verification pilot is something I can propose to London.
刘芳: 这个可以作为一个突破口，但要在政府间框架下做，不能由协会单独对接。我会向部里报告这个提议。
陈立言: 我们组可以出一个中英核查方法学对比的技术报告，12月底前完成，作为试点的基础材料。
周文涛: 总结一下：第一，推动MRV互认和中英核查试点；第二，协会牵头中小企业数据能力建设；第三，研究院出政策建议稿。今天就到这里，谢谢各位。

rows.digest:
刘志强: 人基本到齐了，开始吧。今天就定两件事：第一个诉求是什么，第二个用什么方式提。说白了，这次再散了，下次就没人信我们了。
马海涛: 我跟你讲，龙华这边从7月开始每单基础配送费从5.2降到4.3，超时一次罚3块，雨天补贴也砍了。我在美团龙华三站当了四年队长，没见过这么狠的。
黄丽娟: 仓库这边不一样，问题是工时。我们组上个月人均加班112个小时，夜班补贴每晚30块直接取消了。我2月17日刚升的组长，现在组里一半人说要走。
周敏: 从法律上讲，骑手最大的坑是合同主体。大家签的都是跟第三方外包公司，比如那家‘众包睿达’，不是跟平台。我作为德信律师事务所的劳动法合伙人，建议走事实劳动关系认定，先打社保补缴。
刘志强: 周律师，那仲裁要多久？兄弟们等不起，一个月不跑单房租就交不上。
周敏: 集体仲裁立案到开庭一般45天，加上可能的诉讼得半年以上。从法律上讲，人数超过10人可以按集体争议走，证据越统一越快。有材料发我邮箱 zhoumin@dexin-law.cn，或者打所里座机 +86 755 8632 4410。
马海涛: 半年？我跟你讲，等半年站里的人早换一茬了。我的意见是直接全站停跑一天，周五晚高峰，站长陈国栋那边肯定扛不住。
刘志强: 老马，我理解，但全站停跑太显眼了，第一个被封号的就是你。说白了，我以前在富士康干了七年流水线，2010年那次谁站出来谁先走，我不想再看一次。
林晓: 我补充一下。我是从香港中文大学社工系毕业回来的，在这片做了五年。最有用的其实是证据：每个人每天的单量、时长、罚款截图。我们中心有个开源的记账工具，代码在 github.com/linxiao-labour，大家可以直接用。
黄丽娟: 林老师，仓库的考勤是指纹机，数据在公司手里，我们怎么拿？
林晓: 娟姐，你们可以每天下班拍一张排班表，加上微信工作群里主管喊加班的记录，这些仲裁都认。关键是连续三个月不能断。
周敏: 补一句，从法律上讲，工作群里的加班通知证明力很强，但不要在任何微信群讨论我们今天的组织计划，被截图就是‘煽动’。签授权书一律线下、纸质。
马海涛: 那我的微博 weibo.com/u/7731942205 还发不发？我那个号 @深圳骑手老马 有两万多粉，上次发罚款截图转了三千多。
刘志强: 可以发个人遭遇，不要发集体行动的时间地点。说白了，舆论是筹码，不是武器，先留着。

# Digest (session 2026-09-17)

## T1
- Happy to share it, it's at [link].
- To be fair to the authors, internally we see the same pattern.
- To be fair, I can't share the exact pipeline, but the dedup heuristics were written by Priya Raman on our team and they're aggressive.
- Probably not with exact figures.

## T2
- Concretely, I'll also set up the paraphrase-drop harness;
- I'll draft a one-page proposal;
- I'll release the paraphrase set under CC-BY by [date].
- I saw this in my master's at Universidad de los Andes, our synthetic math set saturated in four months.
- I defended my proposal on [date] and that set was the main deliverable.

## T3
- I'm in the lab at [address] most days, so ping me there or on [phone].
- To be blunt about timelines, I'm on sabbatical from January, so the note needs to go to arXiv before Christmas.
- If I'm being honest, I think both are needed: a private held-out set refreshed quarterly plus paraphrase-drop as the reported metric.
- If I'm being honest, the 31% depends heavily on their 13-gram threshold.
- Labs should publish their decontamination reports.

## T4
- Canary strings failing is a disclosure problem.
- Someone at Mila tried this and their canary strings got scraped within a year.
- To be blunt, if that holds, half the leaderboard deltas from last year are noise.
- To be blunt, that scale effect is the headline the paper missed.

## T5
- But the competitive concern is real: the report reveals the data mix.
- A participant rule in this room: a claim without a released script doesn't count.
- A participant, would Meridian commit to that?
- My direct line is [phone] if it gets stuck.
- The paper claims 31% of GSM8K test items appear near-verbatim in two open pretraining corpora.
- Stems only.
- Because the paper only matches stems, and paraphrased stems slip through.
- That reveals nothing about the mix.
- As the person running pretraining data dedup at Meridian, I can say our filtered mix still had roughly 6% of MMLU questions after decontamination.
- Concretely, a participant, is that 6% before or after you strip answer options?
- A participant, can you get legal sign-off to cite those numbers?
- A participant, what do you think of their perplexity-gap test in section 4?
- With options included it was closer to 2%.

## T6
- Concretely, with a participant set we could compute the accuracy drop on paraphrased versus original.
- Our 70B checkpoint dropped 7.5 points on paraphrased GSM8K, the 8B dropped 3.
- I actually have human paraphrases for 500 GSM8K items from my thesis pilot.
- Let me push back on the framing.
- One caveat: 40 items have ambiguous answers and I'd drop them.
- Templates have their own problem, Dr.
- Let me push back again: the perplexity gap between original and paraphrased items is confounded by paraphrase quality.
- Let me push back on that plan: we build a dynamic benchmark, regenerated monthly from templates, so contamination is impossible by construction.
- You need human paraphrases as a control.
- I'll try to get at least relative numbers cleared, 70B versus 8B drop ratio rather than raw accuracy.

## T7
- To be fair, I'd personally support it.
- As director of the Centre, I'd want us to write a response note around it.
- I'd rather we not depend on proprietary numbers at all.

## T8
- Thanks, a participant, I'll take the related-work section.
- I've been pushing for it since I moved here from Beijing last October.
- That's usually acceptable to our reviewers.
- When I reran it at 8-grams last week it jumped to 44%, at 20-grams it dropped to 12%.
- Email me at [email] and I'll route it to our publications review, they usually take two weeks.

## T9
- Right, let's start.
- Sure.
- A participant.
- They used GPT-style rewrites, which are systematically lower-perplexity.
- Contact is [email].
- my student [handle] can circulate it on the workshop Slack.
- We ran something similar.
- Good.

## T10
- If a model loses more than 10 points, that's a stronger signal than any n-gram count.
- Bigger models memorize more, which is the uncomfortable part for us.
- N-gram overlap measures exposure, not memorization.
- Models learn the template distribution.
- Agreed, with one condition: we report results at three n-gram thresholds, not one.
- Decision: we write it, paraphrase-drop is the primary metric, n-gram overlap goes in the appendix.
- Then report aggregate overlap rates per benchmark, not sources.
- Thanks, a participant, for the sweep, but a 32-point swing tells me the metric is unstable, not that contamination is everywhere.

# Digest (session 2026-09-20)

## T1
- 我在青禾读书会做了六年发起人，第一次见大家这么焦虑。
- 我的工作邮箱 [email]，数据看板在 [链接]，大家可以申请权限。

## T2
- 出版也一样，把译者全砍了，出了事谁兜底？
- [参与者]的《雾港纪事》要是加了这一条，我们法务第一个跳起来。
- 马尔克斯的《百年孤独》2011年拿到正式中文授权以后卖了几百万册，靠的是品牌和营销，不是每一个句子。
- 刘宇昆那译本加了多少注，调了多少语序，机翻能整明白吗？
- 奥威尔的《1984》中文版有二十多个译本，读者会比较译者；
- 算我的还是算机器的？
- 说到底，我最担心的是署名。
- 英文版是刘宇昆翻的，2015年拿了雨果奖，那种再创造，机器做不了。
- 那就看法律怎么说。
- 我同意[参与者]。
- 怎么说呢，今天的题目有点敏感：AI翻译进了出版流程以后，译者和作者还剩多少位置。
- 怎么说呢，我提个折中：机翻只用于初稿和样章评估，正式出版必须由署名译者全程负责，稿费不低于千字120。
- 说到底，作者根本不知道自己签了什么。
- 第二，机翻只用于初稿和样章，正式出版稿费不低于千字120；
- 怎么说呢，大家都爱拿刘慈欣的《三体》举例。
- 我从作者这边说。
- 我在豆瓣的号 [账号] 发过全过程。
- 那我这边的合同，‘衍生技术使用’这条我要求单列，AI有声书另签。
- 呵呵，‘衍生技术使用’，这措辞可真是高明，写了跟没写一样。
- 我去年在大连外国语大学带过一学期翻译工作坊，学生拿机翻改《三体》片段，全给整拧巴了。
- 我那本《雾港纪事》去年加印时，出版方问能不能授权做AI有声书和机翻英文样章，合同里一句‘衍生技术使用’就带过了。
- 怎么说呢，[日期]前把草稿发我邮箱 [邮箱]。
- 不过提醒一句，倡议发出去，可别又是喝杯茶就散了，呵呵。
- 行，那我整一份机翻错误对照表，《三体》片段那份也放进去，让大伙儿瞅瞅机器到底差在哪。
- 那去年豆瓣上被骂到2.9分的那个机翻版又是谁家的？

## T3
- [参与者]，这玩意儿咋整？
- 我经纪人小罗下周会联系[参与者]，她手机 [电话]。
- [参与者]的眼光可真是独到。
- [参与者]这算盘打得可真响，佩服佩服。

## T4
- 另外，韩江拿了2024年诺贝尔文学奖以后，她的英译者黛博拉·史密斯被反复拿出来讨论，说明译者本身就是作品价值的一部分。
- 这事儿得整明白：机翻部分要是不受保护，那精修以后的译文算谁的？
- 2021年施行的新修订《著作权法》对AI生成内容其实没有明确规定；
- 马斯克收购推特以后裁掉了大半内容审核团队，结果大家都看到了。
- 美国版权局倒是表过态，纯AI生成的部分不受版权保护。
- 这事儿老鼻子人遇到过，就是不敢吭声。

## T5
- 我建议合同里强制写明：AI参与程度和精修人员姓名都要印在版权页上。
- 平台这边我可以推一个‘人工译者认证’标签，有标签的书首页给流量。
- 普通类型小说的读者不挑，只要通顺就行。
- 第一，联合出一份《AI翻译使用倡议》，要求版权页标明AI参与程度和译者姓名；
- 这个标签我们能接受。
- 我[地址]，样书寄那边就行。
- 我们今年引进的12本外国小说里，有4本试了机翻加人工精修，单本翻译费从9万降到3万6。
- 第三，星河平台试点人工译者认证标签。
- 版权归属先放一边，平台这边更现实。
- 精修费按千字80算，比原来千字150少了一半多，可活儿一点没少，机翻那译文错得老鼻子了，我改一页得整半个钟头。
- 我们星河数字阅读平台的合同模板我看过，这一条一般藏在第十七条的附件里。
- 呵呵，读者不挑？

## T6
- 讲句实在话，版权页署‘AI辅助’会影响首印量，渠道一看就压价。
- 讲句实在话，不是我们不给钱，是市场不给钱。
- 讲句实在话，成本压力是真的。
- 讲句实在话，《三体》是特例。
- 我这人实在，有事打我电话 [电话]，我把改过的稿子逐句对比给你们看。
- 讲句实在话，如果有流量补贴，机翻精修的书我们可以主动标注‘AI辅助’，新书书讯里也写清楚。

## T7
- 人齐了，咱们开始。
- 我没意见。
- 好，我总结。
- 说得对。
- 可不咋的。

## T8
- 难道我们不想用好译者吗？
- 可如果机翻精修只署‘编辑部’，译者这个职业就被抹掉了。
- 纸书码洋这三年掉了快三成，难道让我自掏腰包？
- 我作为蓝鲸文化的副总编辑，签字的就是我。
- 我[日期]刚跟出版社打完官司，就因为译者名被印成了封底小字。
- 呵呵，打官司，勇气可嘉。

# Digest (session 2026-09-24)

## T1
- In our spring survey, 71% of undergraduates said they'd used ChatGPT on coursework at least once, and only 18% thought they'd broken a rule.
- Five: staff tools only through university-contracted services.

## T2
- Any staff tool needs a university contract.
- Separately, staff use.
- If a student complains that a tier was unfair, the module convenor shouldn't carry it alone.
- I'd just gently note the workload.
- Speaking as a writer, I'd also want a short reflective note on process for any tier-two assignment: what the tool suggested, what you kept, what you rejected.
- I'd just gently add that detection tools are not the answer.
- I'd just gently propose a three-tier model per assignment: AI prohibited, AI permitted with disclosure, AI required.
- I'd just gently ask that the policy protect junior staff too.
- The EU AI Act classifies AI systems used to evaluate students or determine admissions as high-risk, so any grading tool we adopt will carry compliance obligations from 2026.
- Each syllabus marks every assignment with one tier, and students attach a short disclosure statement when they use it.
- Students should understand that these tools are built on other people's unpaid work.
- Four: process notes for tier two.
- That suggests oral defence as the safeguard rather than detection.

## T3
- Two: no AI detectors in misconduct cases.
- With respect, if we let students run prompts on everything, we're teaching them that authorship is optional.
- With respect, it'll be the international students, which is the same bias a participant described with detectors.
- With respect, put that in the minutes too.
- From where I sit at the Centre for Teaching and Learning, the existing code is simply not being read that way.
- With respect, students have to learn to write a paragraph unaided before they learn to edit a machine's.
- The Centre can fund graduate assistants to run them.
- With respect, students will tick 'no AI' and move on.
- With respect, we already have an academic integrity code.

## T4
- And for the record, I won't be using The Salt Archive as a set text again until the publisher clarifies the licensing, so it's off the reading list either way.
- For what it's worth, the legal side is moving.
- When my novel The Salt Archive came out in translation last year, I found pirated copies of it in a training dataset scrape.
- A participant The Salt Archive is exactly why I'm against blanket permission.
- For what it's worth, I've chaired this department for eight years and I've never seen a policy question split us this badly.
- I set it up after moving over from the Toronto school board in 2024, and it's already compliant with our data protection review.

## T5
- Oh brilliant, another committee to draft another policy that students will ignore.
- My office is [address], if anyone wants to draft that clause with me.
- And GDPR applies to anything students paste in.
- Item one is the generative AI policy, which the Dean wants by November.
- Oh, and what a joy, another policy review in twelve months, I assume.

## T6
- For what it's worth, the Russell Group published principles on generative AI in 2023 that lean the same way: teach AI literacy, adapt assessment, don't ban.
- call [phone] if it's urgent.
- we don't need a new document.

## T7
- I'll circulate on the department Slack as [handle]-lit.
- I'd just gently volunteer to draft the tier definitions.
- One: three-tier labels on every assignment, tier one default in first year.
- Drop me a line at [email] and I'll send the costing.
- I'll second that.
- Draft to me at [email] by [date];
- And I'll draft the first-year clause.
- I'll concede the tiers if tier one, AI prohibited, is the default for all first-year writing modules.

## T8
- AI-written essays are plagiarism under the existing wording;
- Splendid, so now every essay comes with a confession form.

## T9
- We could sample instead: viva 15% of submissions at random plus any flagged by the marker's judgement.
- Because nothing says rigorous scholarship like a checkbox.
- Speaking as a writer, my worry is different.
- OpenAI itself withdrew its AI text classifier in 2023 because of low accuracy, and the false-positive studies show non-native English writers get flagged far more often.
- Fine.
- Agreed.
- Let's get going.
- Then make it purely random, no discretionary flags.
- we shouldn't build marking workflows on a vendor whose terms might flip next term.
- My agent someone is chasing it.
- Who exactly do you think gets 'flagged by judgement' first?
- Three: random 15% vivas, funded by the Centre.
- Good.
- Musk buying Twitter showed how fast a platform's terms can change;
- the conversation is.
- Random vivas.
- Right, decisions.
- Wonderful.
- Orwell's 'Politics and the English Language' argues that sloppy language enables sloppy thinking.
- Marvellous.

## T10
- I'm up for tenure review in March, and I can't absorb that on top of my teaching load.
- A participant, the checkbox isn't the point;
- That's the part people forget.
- Quick data point.
- That's fair.
- That's the lesson: if a student can't defend a sentence in a viva, they didn't write it.
- If a student uploads a classmate's peer review into a chatbot, that's personal data leaving the university.
- A ten-minute viva for each of 140 students in my second-year module is twenty-three hours.
- We have a sandboxed instance at [link] that doesn't retain data.

# Digest (session 2026-09-16)

## T1
- 影像科的预约有问题可以打我手机[电话]，晚上也能接。
- 我来汇报影像。
- [参与者]说得对，EBUS大概一周能排上。
- 补充一下，我[日期]刚轮转到影像科，这个片子是和[某人]老师一起复核的，7组我们俩意见不完全一致。
- 好，联系方式我确认一下：患者本人电话[电话]，住[地址]，主要联系人是他女儿赵晓雯。

## T2
- [账号] 是我的科室群账号，结果出来直接在群里[账号]。
- 他有20年吸烟史，每天一包，基线肺纤维化要排除，否则免疫性肺炎风险高。
- 那我先把免疫治疗前的基线检查开了：甲功、皮质醇、心肌酶、肺功能。
- 病理这边，CT引导穿刺是浸润性腺癌，腺泡为主。
- 我先交代一句，我们中国医学科学院肿瘤医院胸外科这边已经评估过心肺功能，FEV1 2.1升，DLCO 78%，肺叶切除没问题。
- 问题是4R没有病理证实，严格讲N2是影像学推断的。

## T3
- 我可以接受这个分支。
- 我写的勾画模板放在[链接]上了，需要可以参考。
- 我平时在[链接]发一些病理科普，MPR取材规范也写过一篇，年轻医生可以看看。

## T4
- [参与者]你放心。
- 各位，今天讨论的病例是[某人]，男，61岁，身份证[证件号]，[日期]入院。
- 九周后MDT再讨论一次，谢谢[参与者]、[参与者]、[参与者]和[参与者]。

## T5
- 但多站N2也有ESMO数据支持新辅助后手术，坦率讲指南给的是2B类，不是禁忌。
- 我上个月刚从MD安德森进修回来，那边分期不清楚的N2基本都要求EBUS，ROSE现场评估一次就能拿到够用的组织。
- EBUS标本我要求至少三针，一针做ROSE，两针留NGS补测，KRAS G12C和MET 14外显子跳跃这次没覆盖到，要补。
- 最后总结：先EBUS分期；
- 坦率讲，这周最好定下来，病人家属很焦虑。
- 坦率讲，他体能状态ECOG 0，能手术就别放弃手术机会。
- 单站N2走三周期新辅助免疫化疗后手术；
- 远处没看到转移，头颅MRI阴性。
- 但组织条只有两条，EGFR、ALK用NGS测了阴性，PD-L1 22C3 TPS 60%。
- 坦率讲，驱动基因阴性、PD-L1 60%，这是新辅助免疫联合化疗最受益的人群。

## T6
- 不过SUV 3.1确实卡在边上，我同意穿刺确认。
- 4R组淋巴节短径1.4厘米，SUV 6.8，7组SUV 3.1，可疑。
- 这点请[参与者]记录在会诊意见里。
- 方案和知情同意书我发邮件给大家，[邮箱]，有意见直接回。

## T7
- [参与者]，PACIFIC那批病人大部分不可切除，跟这个病人不是一回事。
- 多站N2做完新辅助我们也不一定切得干净。
- 所以我坚持，先做EBUS-TBNA，把4R和7组都穿一下。
- 如果EBUS证实4R和7组双阳性，我希望这个病例转回放疗科评估，不要硬上新辅助再手术。
- 说白了，三周期后如果降期到N0或单站N1，我们就做胸腔镜右上肺叶切除加系统性淋巴结清扫。
- 说白了，就是想定一下这个病人先手术还是先做新辅助。
- 作为放疗科副主任，我只是提醒，新辅助后如果pCR没达到，术后还要不要PORT，这个要提前想好，Lung ART的结果是阴性的。
- [参与者]，我同意新辅助，但说白了前提是N2得是单站。
- 右上肺尖后段实性结节3.8厘米，PET-CT SUVmax 11.2；
- [参与者]，7组我还是觉得偏炎性，形态是扁的，有脂肪门。
- 我不是反对手术。
- 还有一点，新辅助后的标本请一定送我们这边做主要病理缓解评估，残留活性肿瘤≤10%才算MPR，取材要按IASLC推荐全瘤床取。

## T8
- 从剂量学角度，如果4R加7组都是阳性，就是多站N2，我更建议根治性同步放化疗60Gy/30次，后面接度伐利尤单抗巩固一年，PACIFIC的五年生存43%也不差。
- 多站N2转放疗科评估同步放化疗。
- 疗效评估我建议每两周期复查一次增强CT，按RECIST 1.1，必要时第三周期后再做一次PET。
- CheckMate 816的数据pCR 24%，我倾向三周期纳武利尤单抗加卡铂培美曲塞。
- 从剂量学角度再说一句，如果最后走放化疗，V20要控制在30%以下，他的肺功能扛得住。
- 我那对双胞胎刚上一年级，这两周下午可能要早走，复查读片我会提前排好。

- [参与者]你把联系方式给那位老师。

- Bottom line, make the second tranche conditional on the match actually arriving.
- A county match would actually make this much easier to renew.
- I'd add a caution: county matches in Weining have a history of slipping.
- Our RCT across 96 schools in Yunnan showed retention subsidies cut turnover by 40%, and as a senior fellow at PIRD I've seen the tech-first pilots mostly end up as dusty tablets.
- Bottom line: pay through the county education bureau payroll, not through school principals.

## T6
- Frankly, leakage is the number one killer of cash-transfer programs.
- Frankly, it's a stronger design than what most foundations fund.
- Frankly, the evidence is on the program team's side here.
- One more thing on the digital piece.
- Please loop me in directly, my cell is [phone] while I'm still sorting out a Shanghai number.

## T7
- Is the split 50/20/15 with a 15% reserve?
- 我的方案是60%投教师补贴，25%做数字化课程，15%留给评估和应急。
- 我不同意砍到15%。
- 测评我没意见。
- 15%是57万，够做基线和终期两次测评。
- 那就定下来：教师补贴50%，数字化课程20%，评估15%，应急储备15%；
- [参与者]，评估这块15%够不够？
- 没有反对，但我保留意见：应急储备没花完的部分，第三年必须优先转为补贴接续，这个要写进会议纪要。
- I'd cut the 25% to 15% and go offline-first.
- [参与者]你和[参与者]会后单独对一下数字化的预算明细。

## T8

- 说到底，我们得让钱比冬天先到。
- 有没有反对？
- 说到底，钱不多，不能撒胡椒面。
- 说到底，透明比公关有用。

## T9
- 我同意把第二笔款和配套挂钩。
- 我更倾向后者，配套写进协议。
- 第二笔款以县财政30%配套到位为前提。
- 二是第二年起要求县财政配套30%。

## T10
- 细表我发大家邮箱，有问题直接找我 [邮箱]。
- PIRD can do the external evaluation pro bono for the baseline.
- [参与者]这个问题问得对。
- Send me the draft at [email] and I'll mark it up.

## T11
- 账面上看，有两条路：一是用我们的留本基金收益，每年大概40万；
- [参与者]，你算一下如果补贴降到50%，第三年用什么接上。
- 账面上看，发放环节的风控比比例更要紧。
- 账面上看，60%做补贴等于每年228万的经常性支出，这笔钱只有两年期限，第三年补贴断了老师照样走。

## T12
- 好，人到齐了我们开始。
- 好的，让她直接打我手机[电话]，我这周都在毕节。
- 我上个月刚从哥伦比亚TC读完在职硕士，论文就是做离线课程的，内容制作的成本主要在前期，砍了就做不出完整的三年级数学包。
- Agreed.
- 走教育局工资系统我们试过，到账要拖三个月。
- 这个我来处理，我用[账号]。
- 补贴由基金会直发、季度核对；
- Before we close, I need a decision I can take back.
- 那我提个折中：补贴由基金会直接打卡，但每季度要和教育局在岗名单核对。

## T13
- I joined Hollis Family Trust only in June, but our board already asked me why the 2024 cohort reported no test-score data.
- From where we sit, the trust cares about measurable learning outcomes, not just headcount.
- From where we sit, quarterly reconciliation would satisfy our compliance team.
- My daughter just started at a boarding school in Kunming, and frankly the offline video lessons there work far better than the live-streamed ones.
- Our trustees meet on [date].
- From where we sit, a co-funding commitment is the strongest signal of sustainability we can show our trustees.

# Digest (session 2026-09-22)

## T1
- But residential retrofit is left to member states, and that's exactly where the bottleneck is.
- The World Health Organization's housing and health guidelines link cold indoor temperatures to excess winter deaths, so insulation retrofits are a health policy too.

## T2
- [参与者]提到的是原地安置率。
- [参与者]说得有道理。

## T3
- 这个思路跟市里的方向一致。
- 我先讲市里的口径。
- 不过财政口径要跟省里对齐，我下周去省发改委汇报。

## T4
- 老实讲，我只希望议事会唔系摆设。
- 我细个喺深水埗长大，见过太多旧楼重建之后原居民根本返唔来。
- 三分之二这个门槛，从数据上看是合理的。
- 从数据上看，住建部2021年发布的《关于在实施城市更新行动中防止大拆大建问题的通知》规定拆除建筑面积原则上不应大于现状总建筑面积的20%，就是在回应这个。
- 我在市发改委分管能源这块三年，最难的就是物业不愿意担责任。
- 从数据上看，国家统计局公布2024年新能源汽车产量超过1300万辆，需求已经不是问题，问题在落地。
- 老实讲，居民那边问题唔系技术，系车位。
- 从数据上看，共享桩的利用率能到多少？

## T5
- 滨江的海湾片区唔好再行呢条路。
- 我嘅公众号 [账号] 会跟进，但唔会点名。
- 第四，更新项目设居民议事会，三分之二住户同意才动工。
- 我们做过模拟，门槛到75%以上项目基本推不动，低于50%就会出群体投诉。
- 我研究的那个片区，我自己也住在里面，海湾路36弄，所以感受很直接。
- To be honest，政府愿意签五年运营协议，我们就愿意先垫资，第一批做三个小区。
- 国务院《新能源汽车产业发展规划（2021—2035年）》提出要加快充换电基础设施建设，我们滨江今年的目标是老旧小区新增8000个公共充电桩，财政按每桩补贴2000元。
- [参与者]的演讲稿当然写得漂亮，佢讲‘温度’，街坊感受到的是‘温度计’——一量就知冷暖。
- 按度电补贴这个思路我们可以研究。
- 五年协议要过人大财经委，我尽量争取。
- [参与者]那篇《城市更新要有温度》讲得好好听，但落到楼下就是吵架。
- 第一，充电桩补贴从按桩改为按度电，挂钩利用率；
- 老实讲，我建议每个更新项目设居民议事会，方案要有三分之二住户签字同意先至可以动工。
- 我去年在市委党校讲《城市更新要有温度》的时候也说过，改造要算碳账，也要算民生账。
- 说到城市更新，老实讲，拆了建、建了拆，街坊早就怕了。
- 今天两个议题：新能源车充电设施怎么进老旧小区，以及城市更新里居民怎么参与。
- 我们学院去年在滨江大学周边做过调查，私桩平均每天空置18个小时。
- 有方案可以发我办公室邮箱 [邮箱]。

## T6
- 所以我们打算推‘共享桩’：私人桩错峰开放，物业统一结算。
- 老小区一百户才二十个车位，装了桩谁用？
- 第二，私桩错峰共享，物业统一结算；
- 所以我建议改造和储能打包：外墙保温、屋顶光伏、楼下储能柜一起做。
- 我们启澜储能做的就是社区侧储能柜，白天谷电存、晚上放。
- 老小区变压器容量普遍只有400千伏安，晚上七点一齐充，跳闸是分分钟的事。
- 数据我们可以提供，储能柜的运行数据实时上传到 [链接]。

## T7
- Oh great，又一个试点。

# Digest (session 2026-09-17)

## T1
- If your members have specific questions, email me at [email] or call the economic section on [phone].
- Thanks, a participant.
- I'd strongly advise members not to rely on it.

## T2
- 我同意[参与者]的看法。
- [参与者]，我不太同意。

## T3
- 说白了，没有绿电价格支持，电炉转型就是空话。
- 说白了，还有一个出路是转口和产业转移。
- 协会会向发改委提绿电直供的试点建议。
- 说白了，大厂没问题，中小厂一塌糊涂。
- 说白了，钢铁是第一个挨刀的。

## T4
- Linking is on the table;
- 我手机[电话]，[参与者]你那边能不能牵个线，请英国钢铁协会的人来？
- 这个可以作为一个突破口，但要在政府间框架下做，不能由协会单独对接。
- Frankly, the UK is launching its own CBAM in January 2027, so as first secretary at the British Embassy I'm here partly to listen.
- CBAM明年[日期]进入definitive period，今天主要讨论钢铁出口怎么应对。
- 那英国的UK CBAM会不会和欧盟做linking？

## T5
- 我们研究院的建议稿会写三点：争取过渡期延长、要求方法学互认、把CBAM收入的一部分用于支持发展中国家减排。
- 我会向部里报告这个提议。
- That route worries Brussels most.
- 总结一下：第一，推动MRV互认和中英核查试点；
- 我们组可以出一个中英核查方法学对比的技术报告，12月底前完成，作为试点的基础材料。
- 我们钢协摸底了127家，能出第三方核查报告的不到40家。
- 宝武的[某人]副总上周还跟我说，核查费一家就要30万。
- 我们研究院建议推动中欧在MRV方法学上互认，而不是被动接受default values。
- 第三，研究院出政策建议稿。
- 我们院打算做一个公开的企业碳足迹计算工具，进展我会在[链接]上更新，大家也可以关注[账号]。
- 我们应该在COP31和中欧经贸高层对话上把它定性为单边贸易措施。
- 我[日期]刚调到研究院，之前在条法司做WTO争端。
- [地址]，会后材料我会发到群里。
- I spent six years at DG TAXUD before this posting, so I know how Brussels thinks about default values.

## T6
- 模型和数据都放在[链接]上了。
- 我上个月刚结束在鲁汶大学的访问学者回来，欧方学者普遍认为免费配额比例才是谈判焦点，而不是碳价绝对值。
- 坦率讲，CBAM在WTO框架下有GATT第20条的空间，起诉胜算不大，更现实的是谈判换取全国碳市场价格的抵扣认可。
- 两条腿走路：一边谈判，一边帮中小企业建数据体系。
- 坦率讲，默认值本身就有问题。
- 钢铁纳入全国碳市场预计2027年开始配额分配。
- 从计量角度看，问题在于数据颗粒度。
- 从计量角度看，拒绝合规的代价是企业直接按默认值交钱，2026年就是真金白银的损失。
- 坦率讲，合规越顺利，等于默认了这个机制的合法性。

## T7
- [参与者]我插一句私事：我女儿今年刚去鹿特丹读港口物流，她说欧洲进口商已经开始要求中国供应商提前报碳数据了，市场比政策走得快。
- [参与者]这个称呼我在欧洲用惯了，哈哈。

## T8
- 我们组的测算显示，如果企业能提交实测排放数据，平均碳强度是每吨钢1.9吨CO2，比欧盟默认值低约18%。
- 第二，协会牵头中小企业数据能力建设；
- 补一个数据：电炉钢的碳强度只有长流程的三分之一，如果对欧出口转向电炉钢产品，CBAM成本能降低60%以上，这是结构性答案。
- 欧盟用的是本国排放最差10%的水平，对中国企业带有惩罚性。
- 作为副秘书长我直接给数字：2025年对欧钢材出口大约380万吨，按默认值算，每吨要多付60到90欧元，长流程企业利润基本被吃光。
- [参与者]，你们协会的会员企业有多少真正具备实测核算能力？
- 电炉钢的问题是废钢不够、电价太高。

## T9
- 各位好，今天按Chatham House规则。
- A joint UK-China verification pilot is something I can propose to London.
- 今天就到这里，谢谢各位。
- 已经有企业在越南、马来西亚建轧钢线，把最终加工放在第三国，但欧盟反规避条款会盯上，风险很大。
- 我反对把重点放在合规上。
- 如果英欧两套核算规则不一样，企业合规成本要翻倍。
- 这是关键。
- 这恰恰说明欧方规则在不断扩张。
- Dr.
- 我提个具体要求：协会想办一个中英CBAM合规对接会，11月在唐山。
- The anti-circumvention clause covers slight modifications in third countries.

## T10
- China's ETS allowance price is around 90 yuan, versus 70-plus euros in the EU.
- On the carbon price deduction: the EU will only credit an explicit carbon price actually paid.
- Frankly, the gap is too big for a meaningful deduction unless steel enters the national ETS soon.
- ministers will decide after the ETS linking talks conclude.
- Frankly, bottom line from our side: the UK wants a predictable, data-based system and is open to technical cooperation on MRV.

# Digest (session 2026-09-17)

## T1
- Happy to share it, it's at [link].
- To be fair to the authors, internally we see the same pattern.
- To be fair, I can't share the exact pipeline, but the dedup heuristics were written by Priya Raman in their organisation and they're aggressive.
- Probably not with exact figures.

## T2
- Concretely, I'll also set up the paraphrase-drop harness;
- I'll draft a one-page proposal;
- I'll release the paraphrase set under CC-BY by [date].
- I saw this in my master's at an organisation, our synthetic math set saturated in four months.
- I defended my proposal on [date] and that set was the main deliverable.

## T3
- I'm in the lab at [address] most days, so ping me there or on [phone].
- To be blunt about timelines, I'm on sabbatical from January, so the note needs to go to arXiv before Christmas.
- If I'm being honest, I think both are needed: a private held-out set refreshed quarterly plus paraphrase-drop as the reported metric.
- If I'm being honest, the 31% depends heavily on their 13-gram threshold.
- Labs should publish their decontamination reports.

## T4
- Canary strings failing is a disclosure problem.
- Someone at Mila tried this and their canary strings got scraped within a year.
- To be blunt, if that holds, half the leaderboard deltas from last year are noise.
- To be blunt, that scale effect is the headline the paper missed.

## T5
- But the competitive concern is real: the report reveals the data mix.
- A participant rule in this room: a claim without a released script doesn't count.
- A participant, would an organisation commit to that?
- My direct line is [phone] if it gets stuck.
- The paper claims 31% of GSM8K test items appear near-verbatim in two open pretraining corpora.
- Stems only.
- Because the paper only matches stems, and paraphrased stems slip through.
- That reveals nothing about the mix.
- In practice, I can say our filtered mix still had roughly 6% of MMLU questions after decontamination.
- Concretely, a participant, is that 6% before or after you strip answer options?
- A participant, can you get legal sign-off to cite those numbers?
- A participant, what do you think of their perplexity-gap test in section 4?
- With options included it was closer to 2%.

## T6
- Concretely, with a participant set we could compute the accuracy drop on paraphrased versus original.
- Our 70B checkpoint dropped 7.5 points on paraphrased GSM8K, the 8B dropped 3.
- I actually have human paraphrases for 500 GSM8K items from my thesis pilot.
- Let me push back on the framing.
- One caveat: 40 items have ambiguous answers and I'd drop them.
- Templates have their own problem, Dr.
- Let me push back again: the perplexity gap between original and paraphrased items is confounded by paraphrase quality.
- Let me push back on that plan: we build a dynamic benchmark, regenerated monthly from templates, so contamination is impossible by construction.
- You need human paraphrases as a control.
- I'll try to get at least relative numbers cleared, 70B versus 8B drop ratio rather than raw accuracy.

## T7
- To be fair, I'd personally support it.
- In their role, I'd want us to write a response note around it.
- I'd rather we not depend on proprietary numbers at all.

## T8
- Thanks, a participant, I'll take the related-work section.
- I've been pushing for it since I moved here from Beijing last October.
- That's usually acceptable to our reviewers.
- When I reran it at 8-grams last week it jumped to 44%, at 20-grams it dropped to 12%.
- Email me at [email] and I'll route it to our publications review, they usually take two weeks.

## T9
- Right, let's start.
- Sure.
- A participant.
- They used GPT-style rewrites, which are systematically lower-perplexity.
- Contact is [email].
- my student [handle] can circulate it on the workshop Slack.
- We ran something similar.
- Good.

## T10
- If a model loses more than 10 points, that's a stronger signal than any n-gram count.
- Bigger models memorize more, which is the uncomfortable part for us.
- N-gram overlap measures exposure, not memorization.
- Models learn the template distribution.
- Agreed, with one condition: we report results at three n-gram thresholds, not one.
- Decision: we write it, paraphrase-drop is the primary metric, n-gram overlap goes in the appendix.
- Then report aggregate overlap rates per benchmark, not sources.
- Thanks, a participant, for the sweep, but a 32-point swing tells me the metric is unstable, not that contamination is everywhere.

# Digest (session 2026-09-24)

## T1
- In our spring survey, 71% of undergraduates said they'd used ChatGPT on coursework at least once, and only 18% thought they'd broken a rule.
- Five: staff tools only through university-contracted services.

## T2
- Any staff tool needs a university contract.
- Separately, staff use.
- If a student complains that a tier was unfair, the module convenor shouldn't carry it alone.
- I'd just gently note the workload.
- Speaking as a writer, I'd also want a short reflective note on process for any tier-two assignment: what the tool suggested, what you kept, what you rejected.
- I'd just gently add that detection tools are not the answer.
- I'd just gently propose a three-tier model per assignment: AI prohibited, AI permitted with disclosure, AI required.
- I'd just gently ask that the policy protect junior staff too.
- The EU AI Act classifies AI systems used to evaluate students or determine admissions as high-risk, so any grading tool we adopt will carry compliance obligations from 2026.
- Each syllabus marks every assignment with one tier, and students attach a short disclosure statement when they use it.
- Students should understand that these tools are built on other people's unpaid work.
- Four: process notes for tier two.
- That suggests oral defence as the safeguard rather than detection.

## T3
- Two: no AI detectors in misconduct cases.
- With respect, if we let students run prompts on everything, we're teaching them that authorship is optional.
- With respect, it'll be the international students, which is the same bias a participant described with detectors.
- With respect, put that in the minutes too.
- From where I sit at the an organisation, the existing code is simply not being read that way.
- With respect, students have to learn to write a paragraph unaided before they learn to edit a machine's.
- The Centre can fund graduate assistants to run them.
- With respect, students will tick 'no AI' and move on.
- With respect, we already have an academic integrity code.

## T4
- And for the record, I won't be using a work as a set text again until the publisher clarifies the licensing, so it's off the reading list either way.
- For what it's worth, the legal side is moving.
- When my novel a work came out in translation last year, I found pirated copies of it in a training dataset scrape.
- A participant a work is exactly why I'm against blanket permission.
- For what it's worth, a participant has relevant leadership experience and I've never seen a policy question split us this badly.
- I set it up after moving over from the Toronto school board in 2024, and it's already compliant with our data protection review.

## T5
- Oh brilliant, another committee to draft another policy that students will ignore.
- My office is [address], if anyone wants to draft that clause with me.
- And GDPR applies to anything students paste in.
- Item one is the generative AI policy, which the Dean wants by November.
- Oh, and what a joy, another policy review in twelve months, I assume.

## T6
- For what it's worth, the Russell Group published principles on generative AI in 2023 that lean the same way: teach AI literacy, adapt assessment, don't ban.
- call [phone] if it's urgent.
- we don't need a new document.

## T7
- I'll circulate on the department Slack as [handle]-lit.
- I'd just gently volunteer to draft the tier definitions.
- One: three-tier labels on every assignment, tier one default in first year.
- Drop me a line at [email] and I'll send the costing.
- I'll second that.
- Draft to me at [email] by [date];
- And I'll draft the first-year clause.
- I'll concede the tiers if tier one, AI prohibited, is the default for all first-year writing modules.

## T8
- AI-written essays are plagiarism under the existing wording;
- Splendid, so now every essay comes with a confession form.

## T9
- We could sample instead: viva 15% of submissions at random plus any flagged by the marker's judgement.
- Because nothing says rigorous scholarship like a checkbox.
- Speaking as a writer, my worry is different.
- OpenAI itself withdrew its AI text classifier in 2023 because of low accuracy, and the false-positive studies show non-native English writers get flagged far more often.
- Fine.
- Agreed.
- Let's get going.
- Then make it purely random, no discretionary flags.
- we shouldn't build marking workflows on a vendor whose terms might flip next term.
- My agent someone is chasing it.
- Who exactly do you think gets 'flagged by judgement' first?
- Three: random 15% vivas, funded by the Centre.
- Good.
- Musk buying Twitter showed how fast a platform's terms can change;
- the conversation is.
- Random vivas.
- Right, decisions.
- Wonderful.
- Orwell's 'Politics and the English Language' argues that sloppy language enables sloppy thinking.
- Marvellous.

## T10
- a participant faces an upcoming career review, and I can't absorb that on top of my teaching load.
- A participant, the checkbox isn't the point;
- That's the part people forget.
- Quick data point.
- That's fair.
- That's the lesson: if a student can't defend a sentence in a viva, they didn't write it.
- If a student uploads a classmate's peer review into a chatbot, that's personal data leaving the university.
- A ten-minute viva for each of 140 students in my second-year module is twenty-three hours.
- We have a sandboxed instance at [link] that doesn't retain data.

## T1
- 影像科的预约有问题可以打我手机[电话]，晚上也能接。
- 我来汇报影像。
- [参与者]说得对，EBUS大概一周能排上。
- 补充一下，我[日期]刚轮转到影像科，这个片子是和[某人]老师一起复核的，7组我们俩意见不完全一致。
- 好，联系方式我确认一下：患者本人电话[电话]，住[地址]，主要联系人是他女儿赵晓雯。

## T2
- [账号] 是我的科室群账号，结果出来直接在群里[账号]。
- 他有20年吸烟史，每天一包，基线肺纤维化要排除，否则免疫性肺炎风险高。
- 那我先把免疫治疗前的基线检查开了：甲功、皮质醇、心肌酶、肺功能。
- 病理这边，CT引导穿刺是浸润性腺癌，腺泡为主。
- 我先交代一句，[某机构]这边已经评估过心肺功能，FEV1 2.1升，DLCO 78%，肺叶切除没问题。
- 问题是4R没有病理证实，严格讲N2是影像学推断的。

## T3
- 我可以接受这个分支。
- 我写的勾画模板放在[链接]上了，需要可以参考。
- 我平时在[链接]发一些病理科普，MPR取材规范也写过一篇，年轻医生可以看看。

## T4
- [参与者]你放心。
- 各位，今天讨论的病例是[某人]，男，61岁，身份证[证件号]，[日期]入院。
- 九周后MDT再讨论一次，谢谢[参与者]、[参与者]、[参与者]和[参与者]。

## T5
- 但多站N2也有ESMO数据支持新辅助后手术，坦率讲指南给的是2B类，不是禁忌。
- 我上个月刚从[某机构]进修回来，那边分期不清楚的N2基本都要求EBUS，ROSE现场评估一次就能拿到够用的组织。
- EBUS标本我要求至少三针，一针做ROSE，两针留NGS补测，KRAS G12C和MET 14外显子跳跃这次没覆盖到，要补。
- 最后总结：先EBUS分期；
- 坦率讲，这周最好定下来，病人家属很焦虑。
- 坦率讲，他体能状态ECOG 0，能手术就别放弃手术机会。
- 单站N2走三周期新辅助免疫化疗后手术；
- 远处没看到转移，头颅MRI阴性。
- 但组织条只有两条，EGFR、ALK用NGS测了阴性，PD-L1 22C3 TPS 60%。
- 坦率讲，驱动基因阴性、PD-L1 60%，这是新辅助免疫联合化疗最受益的人群。

## T6
- 不过SUV 3.1确实卡在边上，我同意穿刺确认。
- 4R组淋巴节短径1.4厘米，SUV 6.8，7组SUV 3.1，可疑。
- 这点请[参与者]记录在会诊意见里。
- 方案和知情同意书我发邮件给大家，[邮箱]，有意见直接回。

## T7
- [参与者]，PACIFIC那批病人大部分不可切除，跟这个病人不是一回事。
- 多站N2做完新辅助我们也不一定切得干净。
- 所以我坚持，先做EBUS-TBNA，把4R和7组都穿一下。
- 如果EBUS证实4R和7组双阳性，我希望这个病例转回放疗科评估，不要硬上新辅助再手术。
- 说白了，三周期后如果降期到N0或单站N1，我们就做胸腔镜右上肺叶切除加系统性淋巴结清扫。
- 说白了，就是想定一下这个病人先手术还是先做新辅助。
- 以其身份，我只是提醒，新辅助后如果pCR没达到，术后还要不要PORT，这个要提前想好，Lung ART的结果是阴性的。
- [参与者]，我同意新辅助，但说白了前提是N2得是单站。
- 右上肺尖后段实性结节3.8厘米，PET-CT SUVmax 11.2；
- [参与者]，7组我还是觉得偏炎性，形态是扁的，有脂肪门。
- 我不是反对手术。
- 还有一点，新辅助后的标本请一定送我们这边做主要病理缓解评估，残留活性肿瘤≤10%才算MPR，取材要按IASLC推荐全瘤床取。

## T8
- 从剂量学角度，如果4R加7组都是阳性，就是多站N2，我更建议根治性同步放化疗60Gy/30次，后面接度伐利尤单抗巩固一年，PACIFIC的五年生存43%也不差。
- 多站N2转放疗科评估同步放化疗。
- 疗效评估我建议每两周期复查一次增强CT，按RECIST 1.1，必要时第三周期后再做一次PET。
- CheckMate 816的数据pCR 24%，我倾向三周期纳武利尤单抗加卡铂培美曲塞。
- 从剂量学角度再说一句，如果最后走放化疗，V20要控制在30%以下，他的肺功能扛得住。
- 我那对双胞胎刚上一年级，这两周下午可能要早走，复查读片我会提前排好。

- [参与者]这个问题问得对。
- Send me the draft at [email] and I'll mark it up.

- 账面上看，有两条路：一是用我们的留本基金收益，每年大概40万；
- [参与者]，你算一下如果补贴降到50%，第三年用什么接上。

- 好，人到齐了我们开始。

- From where we sit, quarterly reconciliation would satisfy our compliance team.

- 协会会向发改委提绿电直供的试点建议。
- 说白了，大厂没问题，中小厂一塌糊涂。

## T5
- [某机构]的建议稿会写三点：争取过渡期延长、要求方法学互认、把CBAM收入的一部分用于支持发展中国家减排。
- 我会向部里报告这个提议。
- That route worries Brussels most.
- 总结一下：第一，推动MRV互认和中英核查试点；
- [某机构]可以出一个中英核查方法学对比的技术报告，12月底前完成，以其身份。
- 我们[某机构]摸底了127家，能出第三方核查报告的不到40家。

- [某机构]建议推动中欧在MRV方法学上互认，而不是被动接受default values。
- 第三，研究院出政策建议稿。
- [某机构]打算做一个公开的企业碳足迹计算工具，进展我会在[链接]上更新，大家也可以关注[账号]。
- 我们应该在COP31和中欧经贸高层对话上把它定性为单边贸易措施。
- 我[日期]刚调到研究院，有过相关从业经历。
- [地址]，会后材料我会发到群里。
- I spent six years at an organisation before this posting, so I know how Brussels thinks about default values.

## T6
- 模型和数据都放在[链接]上了。
- 我上个月刚结束在[某机构]的[某职务]回来，欧方学者普遍认为免费配额比例才是谈判焦点，而不是碳价绝对值。
- 坦率讲，CBAM在WTO框架下有GATT第20条的空间，起诉胜算不大，更现实的是谈判换取全国碳市场价格的抵扣认可。
- 两条腿走路：一边谈判，一边帮中小企业建数据体系。
- 坦率讲，默认值本身就有问题。

# Digest (session 2026-09-20)

## T1
- 一位参与者在[某机构]有相关从业经历[某职务]；第一次见大家这么焦虑。
- 一位参与者的工作邮箱 [email]；数据看板在 [链接]；大家可以申请权限。

## T2
- 出版也一样，把译者全砍了，出了事谁兜底？
- [参与者]的[某作品]要是加了这一条；与会方法务第一个跳起来。
- 马尔克斯的《百年孤独》2011年；拿到正式中文授权以后卖了几百万册；靠的是品牌和营销；不是每一个句子。
- 刘宇昆那译本加了多少注；调了多少语序；机翻能吗。
- 奥威尔的《1984》中文版有二十多个译本；读者会比较译者。
- 算一位参与者的还是算机器的？
- 说到底，一位参与者最担心的是署名。
- 英文版是刘宇昆翻的；2015年拿了雨果奖；那种再创造；机器做不了。
- 那就看法律怎么说。
- 一位参与者同意[参与者]。
- 怎么说；今天的题目有点敏感；AI翻译进了出版流程以后；译者和作者还剩多少位置。
- 怎么说；一位参与者提个折中；机翻只用于初稿和样章评估；正式出版必须由署名译者全程负责；稿费不低于千字120。
- 说到底，作者根本不知道自己签了什么。
- 第二；机翻只用于初稿和样章；正式出版稿费不低于千字120。
- 怎么说，大家都爱拿刘慈欣的《三体》举例。
- 一位参与者从作者这边说。
- 一位参与者在豆瓣的号 [账号] 发过全过程。
- 那一位参与者这边的合同；‘衍生技术使用’这条一位参与者要求单列；AI有声书另签。
- ‘衍生技术使用’，这措辞高明，写了跟没写一样。
- 一位参与者去年在大连外国语；大学带过一学期翻译工作坊；学生拿机翻改《三体》片段；全给整拧巴了。
- 一位参与者那本[某作品]去年加印时；出版方问能不能授权做AI有声书和机翻英文样章；合同里一句‘衍生技术使用’就带过了。
- 怎么说，[日期]前把草稿发一位参与者邮箱 [邮箱]。
- 不过提醒一句；倡议发出去；可别又是喝杯茶就散了。
- 行；那一位参与者整一份机翻错误对照表；《三体》片段那份也放进去；让机器到底差在哪。
- 那去年豆瓣上被骂到2；9分的那个机翻版又是谁家的。

## T3
- [参与者]，这玩意儿？
- 一位参与者经纪人小罗下周会联系[参与者]；她手机 [电话]。
- [参与者]的眼光独到。
- [参与者]这算盘打得可真响，。

## T4
- 另外；韩江拿了2024年诺贝尔文学奖以后；她的英译者黛博拉·史密斯被反复拿出来讨论；说明译者本身就是作品价值的一部分。
- 这事儿得；机翻部分要是不受保护；那精修以后的译文算谁的。
- 2021年施行的新修订《著作权法；》对AI生成内容其实没有明确规定。
- 马斯克收购推特以后裁掉了大半内容审核团队；结果大家都看到了。
- 美国版权局倒是表过态；纯AI生成的部分不受版权保护。
- 这事儿人遇到过，就是不敢吭声。

## T5
- 一位参与者建议合同里强制写明；AI参与程度和精修人员姓名都要印在版权页上。
- 平台这边一位参与者可以推；一个‘人工译者认证’标签；有标签的书首页给流量。
- 普通类型小说的读者不挑，只要通顺就行。
- 第一；联合出一份《AI翻译使用倡议》；要求版权页标明AI参与程度和译者姓名。
- 这个标签与会方能接受。
- 一位参与者[地址]，样书寄那边就行。
- 与会方今年引进的12本外国小说里；有4本试了机翻加人工精修；单本翻译费从9万降到3万6。
- 第三，[某机构]平台试点人工译者认证标签。
- 版权归属先放一边，平台这边更现实。
- 精修费按千字80算；比原来千字150少了一半多；可活儿一点没少；机翻那译文错得了；一位参与者改一页得整半个钟头。
- 与会方[某机构]的合同模板一位参与者看过；这一条一般藏在第十七条的附件里。
- 读者不挑？

## T6
- 讲句实在话；版权页署‘AI辅助’会影响首印量；渠道一看就压价。
- 讲句实在话，不是与会方不给钱，是市场不给钱。
- 讲句实在话，成本压力是真的。
- 讲句实在话，《三体》是特例。
- 一位参与者这人实在；有事打一位参与者电话 [电话]；一位参与者把改过的稿子逐句对比给你们看。
- 讲句实在话；如果有流量补贴；机翻精修的书与会方可以主动标注‘AI辅助’；新书书讯里也写清楚。

## T7
- 人齐了，与会方开始。
- 一位参与者没意见。
- 好，一位参与者总结。
- 说得对。

## T8
- 难道与会方不想用好译者吗？
- 可如果机翻精修只署‘[某职务]部’；译者这个职业就被抹掉了。
- 纸书码洋这三年掉了快三成；难道让一位参与者自掏腰包。
- 以其身份，签字的就是一位参与者。
- 一位参与者[日期]刚跟出版社打完官司；就因为译者名被印成了封底小字。
- 打官司，。

# Digest (session 2026-09-24)

## T1
- In their spring survey; 71% of undergraduates said they'd used ChatGPT on coursework at least once; and only 18% thought they'd broken a rule.
- Five: staff tools only through university-contracted services.

## T2
- Any staff tool needs a university contract.
- Separately, staff use.
- If a student complains that a tier was unfair; the module convenor shouldn't carry it alone.
- A participant would just gently note the workload.
- Speaking as a writer; a participant would also want a short reflective note on; process for any tier-two assignment; what the tool suggested; what you kept; what you rejected.
- A participant would just gently add that detection tools are; not the answer.
